title: Fantasy football Start ‘Em, Sit ‘Em: 23 players to start or sit in Week 1
description: The first week of the 2026 NFL season is underway and we've already seen two games played. Here's our start/sit advice for your lineup on Sunday.
fullText:
Week 1 of the 2026 NFL season is officially underway, and fantasy football managers already have plenty to think about.

The defending champion Seattle Seahawks opened the season with a Super Bowl rematch against the Patriots, picking up a win. The San Francisco 49ers and Los Angeles Rams squared off in Melbourne, Australia one night later, giving fans an early taste of what promises to be another unpredictable NFL season.

Now, the wait is over for the rest of the league. A full schedule of games is on tap Sunday, followed by the first "Monday Night Football" matchup of the season. With several divisional battles on the schedule, there are plenty of intriguing games – and fantasy storylines.

Of course, Week 1 is always one of the most difficult weeks to navigate in fantasy football. Managers who drafted A.J. Brown or Brock Bowers are already dealing with uncertainty moving forward, while those who landed Jaxon Smith-Njigba or Mike Evans can feel a little more comfortable about their lineups.

With 28 of 32 teams set to take the field Sunday and Monday, fantasy managers have some difficult decisions to make before kickoff. If you're on the fence about who to start, who to sit or which players could make the biggest impact in Week 1, we've got you covered.

Here are our start 'em and sit 'em recommendations for Week 1 of the 2026 fantasy football season:

The Saints are actually better against quarterbacks than most realize, as they allowed the eighth-fewest fantasy points per game (FPPG) to quarterbacks last season. Even so, Goff is close to a must-start given his proven track record of success in Detroit.

Goff has been one of the most consistent quarterbacks in fantasy football the last three seasons, never throwing for fewer than 4,500 yards or 30 touchdowns. That consistency – along with a strong Lions supporting cast that features Amon-Ra St. Brown, Jameson Williams, Sam LaPorta and Jahmyr Gibbs – makes Goff a high-floor start.

Herbert was able to log a strong fantasy season in 2025 despite being pressured a league-high 288 times, per Pro Football Focus. He should have an easier time staying clean in 2026, with tackles Rashawn Slater and Joe Alt in the fold, and that could raise his ceiling.

Even if Herbert's protection doesn't take an immediate step forward, he shouldn't have any issues against the Cardinals. Arizona had a 31.6% pressure rate last year, which ranked 26th in the league, per the NFL's Next Gen Stats. The Cardinals didn't upgrade their edge rush rotation during the offseason, so Herbert should have plenty of time to pick apart a shaky-looking Arizona defense that surrendered 30.75 points per game during the preseason.

Prescott attempted the second-most passes in the NFL last season behind only Bo Nix. The 33-year-old may not be asked to throw quite as much in 2026, as Dallas' defense looks significantly improved from its league-worst unit last year, but he should still do more than enough to be a top-10 fantasy quarterback.

The Giants struggled to contain opposing quarterbacks last season, surrendering the eighth-most FPPG to the position. Prescott threw for 361 yards, two touchdowns and an interception in his lone full outing against New York, so he could be similarly positioned to thrive to open the fantasy season.

The Cowboys spent a lot of resources during the offseason to upgrade their defense, adding players like Rashan Gary, Jalen Thompson and first-round pick Caleb Downs to the fold. Christian Parker, who comes from the Vic Fangio coaching tree, could eventually lead the unit to success, but it may take time to gel early in the season.

If that happens, Dart should be positioned to take advantage of a Cowboys defense that allowed the most FPPG to quarterbacks last season. That included a league-high eight rushing touchdowns to the position, a stat that marries well with Dart's dual-threat capabilities.

The Browns suffered a couple of major losses on defense over the offseason. The aforementioned Garrett was traded to the Rams while defensive coordinator Jim Schwartz left the team after being passed over for Cleveland's head coaching job in favor of Todd Monken.

Despite these departures, the Browns are still returning most of their 2025 starters, and their defense ranked fourth in defensive EPA allowed per play last season, per the NFL's Next Gen Stats. That may make it hard for Lawrence – who was buoyed by an outlier nine rushing touchdowns in 2025 – to find high-level success in his first game of the 2026 campaign.

Mahomes is expected to play in Week 1 of the 2026 NFL season despite tearing his left ACL and LCL during a December 2025 game against the Los Angeles Chargers. The 30-year-old quarterback may need time to shake off the rust, so it's fair to assume he might get off to a slower start than usual in 2026.

Further complicating Mahomes' path toward a productive fantasy day is that the Broncos have one of the NFL's best defenses. They have enjoyed particular success against Mahomes, who hasn't scored multiple touchdowns in a game against the Broncos since 2022, so it's best to steer clear of the two-time MVP.

Bucky is a sleeper entering 2026 after an injury-riddled season. Before his injury, through the first four weeks of 2025, Irving was third among all RBs in receptions (19) and receiving yards per game (48.3). Irving should excel in this one as a receiver and on the ground against the Bengals defense, which allowed the most fantasy points per game to running backs last season.

Cincinnati ranked 32nd in rushing yards allowed (147.1 per game) and 31st in yards per carry allowed (5.21). They added Dexter Lawrence and Jonathan Allen on the defensive line, but don't let that stop you from trusting Bucky in Week 1. This game has the highest projected total of the week (50.5), so there should be plenty of fantasy goodness to be had.

The Texans' new weapon has a strong Week 1 matchup in his debut. The Bills surrendered the eighth-most fantasy points per game to backs a season ago, including the most rushing touchdowns to opposing backfields.

The Texans ranked eighth in RB rush attempts in 2025, so Montgomery should see plenty of opportunities with his new team. He has also ranked top 10 in goal-to-go rush attempts in six of his seven career seasons, so he's likely to find paydirt in this one. He's a rock-solid RB2 for fantasy managers with legitimate touchdown upside.

Williams staked his claim as one of the top breakout stars in 2025 and cashed in during the offseason with a contract extension in Dallas. He should eat in Week 1 against the Giants on "Sunday Night Football" at MetLife. New York traded away Dexter Lawrence and has done little to fill the void he left behind in run defense that ranked 31st against the run in 2025, allowing 145.3 rushing yards per game and the fifth-most fantasy points per game.

Williams is a strong bet to find the end zone this week. In his one game against the Giants last season, he finished as RB4 that week, rushing for 97 yards and one touchdown on 18 carries while reeling in six of seven targets for 33 yards. Williams is a must-start as a staple in one of the league's top offenses.

The Browns' second-year back has some long-term upside, but he gets a horrible matchup in Week 1 against the Jaguars defense that allowed the third-fewest fantasy points per game and the fewest rushing yards to opposing backs last season. Cleveland is a 7.5-point underdog, which suggests they may be forced to abandon the run if they go down early.

This will be Judkins' first game back since suffering a significant injury: a fractured fibula and dislocated right ankle in December. As a large road underdog, it's likely backup running back Dylan Sampson gets more usage than expected as Judkins is eased into action.

Lloyd has catapulted up fantasy rankings and draft boards since Josh Jacobs was placed on the Commissioner's Exempt List. Green Bay hits the road in Week 1 for a tough divisional matchup with the Vikings, who allowed the tenth-fewest fantasy points per game to opposing running backs a season ago.

Green Bay added Kaleb Johnson and has Chris Brooks available to take meaningful snaps as well. A report Tuesday, Sept. 8 indicated the Packers could deploy a committee to start the season, creating a legitimate threat to Lloyd's workload. Lloyd has played only one regular-season game, totaling six carries for 15 yards, and hasn't played an NFL regular-season snap since 2024. Lloyd has no strong track record to trust in Week 1.

The Commanders' second-year back is trending towards becoming a touchdown-dependent option for fantasy managers. With Rachaad White signing in Washington in the offseason, Croskey-Merritt will likely not be on the field during obvious passing situations, so there isn't a strong three-down role until proven otherwise.

Philadelphia finished last season as a respectable run defense, and with a healthy Jalen Carter and Jordan Davis, they pose a challenge for the Commanders' meager offensive line. Croskey-Merritt had also missed some practice time over the last few weeks with a lower-body issue, adding to the chance he splits more work than expected. There's some long-term intrigue if the Commanders can play from ahead, but Croskey-Merritt can be left on the bench in Week 1.

Lemon was the Eagles' No. 20 overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft. The rookie wideout did not have the most impressive of preseason showings: three receptions for three yards and a dropped pass leading to an interception against the Bengals in the Eagles' final exhibition game of the year. Prior to that, he missed time at training camp with a hamstring injury.

But preseason performance alone should not be a reason to panic – let Ja'Marr Chase's struggles in his rookie preseason be a reminder of that. Lemon is slotting in next to the Eagles' projected lead wideout, DeVonta Smith, and is coming off of an outstanding final year in college. His Week 1 matchup against the Commanders is favorable, too. Washington allowed the second-most expected points added (EPA) on passing plays in 2025, and the team did not do enough to improve its pass defense in a convincing way this offseason.

Downs had a down year – no pun intended – in 2025 but appears set for a return to form in 2026. With Michael Pittman Jr. gone to the Steelers, Downs could see a boost in his target share. That's true especially early in the season, as Pittman's projected replacement – Keenan Allen – was a late free agent signing and could need more time to integrate into the Colts' offense.

Baltimore got off to a very slow start last year as its defense struggled to stop opponents' passing attacks. Even by the end of the year, the Ravens had allowed the second-most passing yards per game behind only the Cowboys. Downs (calf) and Colts quarterback Daniel Jones (Achilles) are both on track to play Week 1. They could have a real opportunity to take advantage of Baltimore's shaky passing defense, which could see another slow start as it adjusts to new head coach Jesse Minter's system.

Johnston's 2025 season was a career year for him with 735 receiving yards and eight touchdowns on 51 catches. In 2026, he has even less competition for targets with veteran Keenan Allen departing for Indianapolis in the offseason. Ladd McConkey likely steps back into the Chargers' lead receiver role after finishing second on the team in catches in 2025, but Johnston is right there behind him in the No. 2 role.

Johnston is almost a no-brainer to start against the Cardinals – a team that ranked dead last in success rate allowed on dropbacks in 2025. Even with McConkey around to haul in most of the targets, Johnston should see plenty of looks of his own in his debut in the Chargers' new-look offense, coordinated by new OC Mike McDaniel.

Rice isn't expected to face NFL discipline after spending 30 days in jail this offseason for a violation of his probation. That is not why he should be considered for a bench spot in Week 1.

More relevant is his opponent and the quarterback situation he faces in Week 1. The Broncos boasted one of the best defenses in football last year – particularly against the pass, where they allowed the lowest success rate (38.5%) on dropbacks of any defense. Making things more difficult is for Rice is the fact he likely will be facing off against 2024 Defensive Player of the Year Patrick Surtain II on most of his routes. On top of that, Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes is making his first start back from a torn ACL and LCL he suffered last December. With Mahomes potentially rusty and the Chiefs emphasizing their run game with the signing of reigning Super Bowl MVP Kenneth Walker, Rice might not have a productive first week in 2026.

Moore may be the Bills' new de facto No. 1 wide receiver after his arrival in Buffalo via trade this offseason, but that has not meant much in the post-Stefon Diggs era. In 2025, the Bills' leading receiver, Khalil Shakir, finished with just 719 yards and four touchdowns. That was after a 2024 season in which the leading receiver (Shakir again) had 821 yards and four touchdowns.

Buffalo's more "spread-the-wealth" approach to receiving output that began in 2024 correlated directly with three things: Diggs' departure from the team, Joe Brady's first year as full-time Bills OC and an uptick in rushing play percentage. In 2026, Brady is now the Bills' head coach but will still call plays for the offense.

As if those factors weren't bad enough indicators for Moore's Bills debut, he also has to make it in Houston. The Texans were the league's best team at limiting EPA and the second-best at limiting opponents' success rate on dropbacks. Essentially all of Houston's defensive core is back: Will Anderson Jr., Danielle Hunter, Derek Stingley Jr. Plus, the Texans added safety Reed Blankenship. Moore's first matchup of 2026 does him no favors from a fantasy outlook perspective.

The Saints offense hasn't been as explosive since Drew Brees walked out the door, but fireworks may return in 2026. In the 11 games played with Tyler Shough in 2025, Johnson excelled, posting 11.5 fantasy points per game. He ultimately finished third among all tight ends in the NFL with 889 receiving yards.

Johnson posted career-highs in targets (102), receptions (77) and yards (889) a season ago. There's little target competition outside of Chris Olave, as rookie Jordyn Tyson remains sidelined with a hamstring injury. The Saints are expected to trail in this game which implies a passing game script. Start Johnson against the shaky Lions secondary in a game that has the second-highest total of Week 1 (49.5).

Until proven otherwise, target the Bengals with the tight end they are facing.

Cincinnati allowed the most receptions to opposing tight ends in 2024 and followed that up with an historically bad 2025, allowing the most receptions again and a staggering 17.45 fantasy points per game to the position. Otton isn't a set-it-and-forget-it for most fantasy managers, but he is the top streamer of Week 1. For squads who plan to taxi a tight end off waivers most weeks, Otton should be your target this week.

The Buccaneers open the season on the road against the Bengals in what projects to be the highest-scoring game of the week. With Emeka Egbuka and Jalen McMillan dealing with injuries, Baker Mayfield will likely lean on Chris Godwin and Otton in order to keep pace with the high-powered Bengals offense.

With A.J. Brown out of town, Goedert has an opportunity to be the second option in Philadelphia's offense behind DeVonta Smith. Goedert clearly has the trust of Jalen Hurts: he accounted for 40.9% of the team's targets inside the 10-yard line, which resulted in a career-high 11 TDs in 2025, and there's little reason to believe that number takes a significant dip in 2026 with Brown's 120 vacated targets. Goedert's targets per route when A.J. Brown was on the field was 18.8% over the last two seasons, and that number jumped to 27.1% when Brown was off the field.

The 31-year-old maintains his every-down role in 2026. Rookie first-round pick Makai Lemon will eventually pose a threat to Goedert's usage, but early on, the vet should be started with confidence. Philadelphia hosts the Commanders who surrendered the fourth-most fantasy points per game to tight ends in 2025.

The Giants host the Cowboys on "Sunday Night Football," and Likely should be a key cog for "Big Blue." The 25-year-old is expected to be a focal point in the passing game after following head coach John Harbaugh from Baltimore and signing a $40 million contract. He was stuck behind Mark Andrews on the depth chart with the Ravens but in 10 games without Andrews throughout his first four NFL seasons, he scored seven touchdowns.

The Cowboys allowed the second-most points in 2024, then allowed the most in 2025, yielding a league-high 60 touchdowns. They made sweeping personnel changes across the defense during the offseason but also have a first-time defensive coordinator.

Star wide receiver Malik Nabers' health remains in question and plenty of focus is on the return of Odell Beckham Jr. Likely is one of the most overlooked tight ends in Week 1 and has breakout potential. Start him with confidence.

Kraft would be ranked inside the top five at the position if we knew he had a clean bill of health. After an early season breakout during which he posted 700 yards and 7 touchdowns, he tore his ACL in November. He's on track to play in Week 1 when Green Bay plays Minnesota on the road but recent comments suggest he will be eased back into action.

Romeo Doubs left in free agency, vacating a team-high 83 targets, opening up Kraft as an elite option when healthy. Green Bay signed Jonnu Smith, which could signal that Kraft could be on a snap count. The Brian Flores-coached Vikings defense allowed the sixth-fewest fantasy points to tight ends in 2025. Kraft has the potential to anchor your lineup as the season progresses but proceed with caution this week.

The Buffalo Bills hit the road in Week 1 and open the season against the NFL's No. 1 defense. It's unlikely Kincaid will make a significant mark in this matchup against the Texans. He will continue to split work with Dawson Knox while competing with D.J. Moore for targets.

Kincaid is a breakout candidate in 2026 but temper expectations in Week 1.

title: Where Mets’ Nolan McLean stands in Rookie of the Year race after Subway Series clunker
description: Mets right-hander Nolan McLean gave up a career-high 10 hits in Friday night's loss to the Yankees at Yankee Stadium.
fullText:
NEW YORK — Mets right-hander Nolan McLean took the mound on Friday night at Yankee Stadium as a long shot in the race for the Rookie of the Year Award in the National League.

It was always going to be an uphill climb for him to catch Cincinnati's Sal Stewart, but with a dominant outing against the Yankees, McLean could've taken his case to contend for that prize to another level of legitimacy.

After all, McLean entered play Friday with the fourth-best ERA of any starting pitcher in baseball — not just rookies — since May 25 (2.24). Overall, his 3.06 ERA across 28 starts this year ranked ninth among qualified arms in the National League. Only six other pitchers had more strikeouts than McLean in 2026 (179).

Rather than building more momentum, however, McLean put together a loss that featured one of his worst lines of the year with a few firsts.

McLean gave up five earned runs against the Yankees in a 6-4 loss on a career-high 10 hits over five frames. Cody Bellinger's three-run home run off McLean in the second inning came on a curveball from McLean with two strikes, the first homer he's allowed on that pitch in his big-league career.

While that home run swing from Bellinger was a tip-the-cap moment — McLean wasn't unhappy with the spot at the knees — interim manager Andy Green pointed out postgame that McLean could've done a better job using the entire zone. There were too many pitches that the right-hander left out and over the plate, pitches that the Yankees pounced on early and often.

"Nolan had the opportunity to probably attack in more than he did today," Green said. "You could feel from the beginning [the Yankees] were living out over [the plate]. So it wasn't necessarily his best day. There was opportunity to probably get in more aggressively than he did."

On one hand, that's frustrating for the Mets to see McLean struggle with hitting spots and attacking with his electric stuff. McLean has recognized this summer that his clunkers often correspond to outings where he doesn't execute well enough with hitting his spots or he fails to get ahead in counts.

That said, even with Friday's dud, McLean has been a top starter in the league for the last several months and he clearly has more room to improve heading into next season. His overall numbers this season are still elite, too. McLean now ranks 16th among all qualified starters in ERA (3.24 over 29 starts). His five strikeouts on Friday pushed McLean up to 184 on the season which is 13th in MLB (three ahead of Paul Skenes and two behind Jacob deGrom). Only seven starters have a lower opponents batting average than McLean (.212). All of that should make Mets fans even more encouraged about what McLean's sophomore season will look like, regardless of where he finishes in the Rookie of the Year Award race.

"This outing will irk him because he's a competitor and expects to win every game he steps on the mound," Green said. "His season's been solid. Still think there's another level for him. I think that's the healthiest way to look at your best players, that there's 

What makes the Rookie of the Year Award so appealing for the Mets, beyond the recognition and hardware, is that New York would be rewarded with an extra draft pick if Carson Benge or McLean were to finish in first place. That's part of the Prospect Promotion Incentive, an initiative that was implemented in MLB's last collective bargaining agreement.

With just over two weeks remaining in the regular season, all signs point toward Stewart as the favorite to win in the National League ahead of Benge and Cardinals shortstop JJ Wetherholt. Wetherholt leads the way in Wins Above Replacement in large part because of his defense, Benge has blossomed this summer and has put together an impressive all-around campaign, but Stewart has 31 home runs and 107 RBI, the highest mark in all of MLB.

title: 1 day till Arizona Cardinals' opener: Remembering the 2001 season
description: With only one day until the Arizona Cardinals' 2026 opener, let's look back at their 2001 season.
fullText:
We continue the countdown to the start of the Arizona Cardinals' regular season. Today, Saturday, September 12, is just one day away from the Arizona Cardinals' regular-season opener on Sept. 13 on the road against the Los Angeles Chargers.

With one day until Week 1, let's look back at the 2001 season for the Cardinals.

It was the first year officially as head coach for Dave McGinnis, and the Cardinals went 7-9. They did start the season 2-6 but went on to win five of their final eight games. It was their final season as part of the NFC East.

They were below average on offense and defense, averaging 20th in points scored (18.4 per game) and 22nd in points allowed (21.4 per game).

They were 31st in third-down offense.

One player had a special season. Receiver David Boston was a Pro Bowler and first-team All-Pro. He had 98 receptions for a league-leading 1,598 yards and eight touchdowns. That yardage mark still is a franchise record.

Jake Plummer started every game. He passed for 3,653 yards, 18 touchdowns and 14 interceptions. It was the only season with the Cardinals in which he threw more touchdown passes than interceptions.

Michael Pittman was the Cardinals' leading rusher with 846 yards and five touchdowns.

Linebacker Ronald McKinnon led the defense with 146 total tackles, and safety Kwamie Lassiter was next with 113.

Rob Frederickson was the team leader with four sacks.

Lassiter picked off nine passes that season and broke up 15.

title: Texas Senator Ted Cruz pitches Protect College Sports Act on College GameDay, warns against what will happen without action
description: Senator Ted Cruz sent a dire warning if Congress does not pass the Protect College Sports Act. In about five years, in Cruz’s estimation, football and other sports will be in an unrecognizable state. The biggest things for Cruz are the transfer rules and a hard out on eligibility for college athletes. You get one […]
fullText:
Senator Ted Cruz sent a dire warning if Congress does not pass the Protect College Sports Act. In about five years, in Cruz's estimation, football and other sports will be in an unrecognizable state.

The biggest things for Cruz are the transfer rules and a hard out on eligibility for college athletes. You get one free transfer and five years of eligibility in total, which ends regardless of how many years used once you turn the age of 24. Keeping that in place, along with an even playing field when it comes to NIL, this is the best solution for football, basketball, wone's sports and other Olympic sports, per Cruz.

$19.99 gets you a FULL year of On3 | Rivals national coverage

"There are no rules, and the situation with the transfer portal, where kids go and transfer two, three, four, five times, it's terrible for the game. It's terrible for the players. It's terrible for the schools, and it's terrible for the families," Cruz said on College GameDay. "And so the reason Congress is acting is because Congress created this problem. It was the federal antitrust laws that were used to bring the lawsuits that struck down all the rules, and so the Protect College Sports Act is bipartisan legislation that's very simple.

"It brings order to chaos. It protects the students, protects the student's ability to be compensated to receive name, image, and likeness compensation, I think that's only fair. It's only right."

Cruz is all about NIL and athletes getting compensated what they're worth. However, that's the key phrase. What they're worth and that has to do with revenue sharing and essentially the limitation of a blank checkbook.

"They're producing enormous value with an enormous skill, but it also puts reasonable rules in place," Cruz said. "So, for example, every player gets one free (transfer), not three or five, one (transfer). It puts an eligibility rule that every player has five years of eligibility, not six, seven, eight; five. And it puts a hard end on that at age 24. It lets the schools compete, and it also slows down what we've got right now (which) is a spiral of cost that is bankrupting almost every college program, most college athletic programs.

"They're losing 10s of millions of dollars, and as a result, they're canceling women's programs. They're canceling non-revenue sports. They're canceling Olympic sports. Within three to five years, we're going to see 40 to 50 schools that have competitive football programs, and everyone else goes under. That would be a tragedy."

College sports are important to Cruz and the fabric of the country, as the senator said. While football is the headlining sport in the Protect College Sports Act, everybody will be affected, hopefully in a positive way, with the bill.

"And so I think the reason Congress is going to happen is because college sports is too precious," Cruz said. "We've got to make sure this remains an avenue for opportunity for millions of kids, and we've got to make sure it remains not just football, but also all of women's sports, all of all of the non-revenue sports, all of the Olympic sports. This bill is designed to do all that."

title: Ted Cruz ruthlessly booed on College GameDay while promoting Protect College Sports Act
description: College football fans were not happy to see Senator Ted Cruz stop by the ESPN College GameDay set.
fullText:
ESPN College GameDay is in Austin, Texas, for Week 2 of the college football season, setting up shop for the blockbuster showdown between the top-ranked Ohio State Buckeyes and No. 4 Texas Longhorns.

During one of the show's opening segments, Texas Senator Ted Cruz pulled up to the set to sit down with host Rece Davis to discuss the Protect College Sports Act.

Unfortunately for Senator Cruz, fans on the LBJ lawn only wanted to hear about today's games. When Cruz appeared on set, boos rained out of the crowd.

Cruz's interview was drowned out by the raucous crowd, which routinely broke out into "Ted Cruz sucks!" chants throughout his sitdown.

MORE: College football games on today, Week 2 AP Top 25 TV schedule for Saturday

ESPN had Ted Cruz on 'College GameDay' in a conversation with Rece Davis for nearly 10 minutes. 

Cruz was heavily booed by the crowd — and heard "Ted, you suck!" chants — in Austin. pic.twitter.com/npQesiYMsG

— Awful Announcing (@awfulannouncing) September 12, 2026

Cruz has been an outspoken supporter of the Protect College Sports Act and has been pushing for President Donald Trump to sign it into federal law.

He recently cited College GameDay clips from Nick Saban and Pat McAfee to promote the bill.

U.S. Sen. Ted Cruz speaks during a conference on Energy Permitting Reform at The Stack at Municipal Light Plant on Sept. 3, 2026 in Columbus, Ohio. Credit: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect (Reuters)

The Protect College Sports Act is a bipartisan bill Cruz co-authored with Democratic Senator Maria Cantwell of Washington.

The bill promotes a federal standard for eligibility, NIL, and transfers, limiting players to just five years of eligibility from the time they graduate high school or turn 19. Under the bill, athletes would receive one no-penalty transfer, which would put an end to the current "wild west" transfer portal.

A Senate vote on the Protect College Sports Act is currently scheduled between September 15 and September 23.

College football did not wait long to produce a game with postseason consequences. No. 1 Ohio State visits No. 4 Texas on Saturday in Austin, placing two national-title favorites and their new-season expectations on the same field.

title: Staff score predictions for Clemson’s Week 2 matchup vs. Georgia Southern
description: Here’s what we’re thinking ahead of Clemson’s Week 2 matchup against Georgia Southern.
fullText:
Clemson football returns to Memorial Stadium on Saturday night looking for a much-needed reset.

The Tigers' 2026 season could hardly have started worse, as LSU handed Clemson a 51-10 loss in Baton Rouge, the largest defeat of the Dabo Swinney era. Now Clemson gets its home opener against Georgia Southern, a matchup the Tigers will be heavily favored to win but one they cannot afford to overlook.

Clemson found that out a year ago against another Sun Belt opponent. Troy gave the Tigers all they could handle before Clemson finally took control with 24 unanswered points. Georgia Southern will arrive in Death Valley with an experienced quarterback capable of making things interesting.

Seventh-year quarterback Max Johnson threw for 281 yards in the Eagles' 31-0 Week 1 win over Charleston Southern. Meanwhile, Clemson still has plenty of questions at quarterback after Christopher Vizzina and freshman Tait Reynolds struggled to generate much offense against LSU. Swinney has already confirmed that both will play Saturday.

A comfortable Clemson victory is expected, but after what happened in Baton Rouge, exactly how the Tigers respond may matter almost as much as the final score.

What channel is Clemson vs Georgia Southern on today? Time, TV info

📸 Coley Cleary, USA TODAY NETWORK. https://t.co/OweFYunEWN pic.twitter.com/2auFOgfl1W

Here are our staff predictions for Clemson vs. Georgia Southern.

I don't think Clemson will have as much trouble as people expect here, but they shouldn't have an easy time either. This Clemson team is one of the worst we've seen in some time on paper and they proved it against LSU in Week 1.

I think Greg McElroy said it best, Clemson has recovered from things like this before, they did it just two years against Georgia. While it wasn't a perfect season, they overcame that Week 1 loss and a lot of doubt and proved to be a solid football team. I don't see Georgia Southern being the team to keep that from happening.

Clemson is coming off the most lopsided loss in Dabo Swinney's entire tenure as head coach, so — famous last words — things can't get any worse in Week 2, right? The Tigers struggled mightily in their Week 2 game against Troy last season and needed 24 unanswered points just to beat the Trojans. Unlike then, an 11-point win against a Sun Belt team at home would be considered an improvement  based on what I saw in Week 1. I'm going with the same score prediction as that game against Troy until or unless the Tigers prove me wrong.

Clemson's offensive line struggled mightily against LSU. That's probably the biggest concern for me, outside of the gap in speed and how slow Clemson looked against an elite team. Don't expect a response similar to 2024's win over App State. I have doubts ether Christopher Vizzina or Tait Reynolds can produce those types of numbers. Clemson wins, but it's another ugly one.

title: Cagliari confirm Trepy allowed back in training a month after drowning incident
description: Wonderful news from Cagliari, as striker Yael Trepy received the all clear from doctors to resume training a month on from the drowning scare that left him in a coma.The 20-year-old ran into difficult...
fullText:
Wonderful news from Cagliari, as striker Yael Trepy received the all clear from doctors to resume training a month on from the drowning scare that left him in a coma.

The 20-year-old ran into difficulty in the deep end of a rented pool during a day off in Sardinia on August 16 and was rushed to hospital in critical condition.

CAGLIARI, ITALY – MARCH 07: Yael Trepy of Cagliari reacts during the Serie A match between Cagliari Calcio and Como 1907 at Stadio Sant'Elia on March 07, 2026 in Cagliari, Italy. (Photo by Enrico Locci/Getty Images)

He was placed in an induced coma to help remove all the water from his lungs, and spent 10 days in hospital receiving treatment.

Trepy was allowed to return home to continue under the care of his family and the club's medical staff.

CAGLIARI, ITALY – FEBRUARY 21: Yael Trepy of Cagliari inspect the pitch before the Serie A match between Cagliari Calcio and SS Lazio at Stadio Sant'Elia on February 21, 2026 in Cagliari, Italy. (Photo by Enrico Locci/Getty Images)

A statement released by Cagliari confirmed that he has been given the all clear to resume training with the rest of his teammates after cardiac tests in Milan showed no after-effects of the harrowing experience.

It will be a gradual process to get him back up to speed, so it is not yet clear when he will be able to return to the field.

CREMONA, ITALY – JANUARY 08: Yael Trepy of Cagliari celebrates scoring his team's second goal with teammates during the Serie A match between US Cremonese and Cagliari Calcio at Stadio Giovanni Zini on January 08, 2026 in Cremona, Italy. (Photo by Pier Marco Tacca/Getty Images)

Joining the Cagliari youth academy in 2023, Trepy had started the first competitive match of the season in the Coppa Italia, and was scheduled to play in Serie A before the accident.

title: Chargers' Jim Harbaugh reveals encouraging status of offensive line

fullText:
Chargers head coach Jim Harbaugh is happy to see offensive tackles Rashawn Slater and Joe Alt back on the field together again.

Harbaugh spoke to the media on Friday and said the two stars are 'ready to roll.'

"It's been earned by rehab and training," Harbaugh said.

"Guys just practicing, working together for the last many months. Ready to roll, in a good place."

Slater and Alt did not play in a single snap together in 2025. Slater was ruled out for the entire season in August 2025 due to a torn left patellar tendon. He required surgery and did not play a single snap.

As for Alt, he was held to only six games. He suffered a severe right high ankle sprain in Week 9 that required surgery.

The two star tackles were not available in the playoffs, which hurt the Chargers' chances of potentially making a deep playoff run.

Now that Alt and Slater are healthy, the Chargers have two of the best at their respective positions. Alt and Slater have a chance to be named All-Pros in 2026, especially under new offensive play caller Mike McDaniel.

The two are expected to be two of the best tackles, protecting Justin Herbert snap-in and snap-out, as well as stabilizing what should be an elite running game led by Omarion Hampton.

Alt and Slater's play will be the difference between another good season for the Chargers and potentially one of the best in franchise history.

title: Brian Burns: Giants are ready to exploit weakness at Cowboys' RT position

fullText:
The John Harbaugh era begins in New York on Sunday night. And the Giants are focusing on one potential path to help Harbaugh start his career as the Giants' head coach at 1-0.

The perceived weakness is at the right tackle position, where the Cowboys recently acquired Broderick Jones to compete with Terence Steele.

"I mean, opportunity lies within the game," linebacker Brian Burns said, via Pat Leonard of the New York Daily News. "They're both pros. Not to disrespect anybody's craft or anything like that, but the fact that they are so concerned in that area does, I guess, raise some form of an alert in our minds, as far as like just knowing that they're having struggles. . . . So we can definitely see that as an opportunity to exploit."

Steele is currently listed as the starter. But if the Cowboys had full faith in him, they wouldn't have traded for Jones.

Another potential soft spot has arisen at left guard, where Tyler Smith on injured reserve after thumb surgery.

And the Giants have plenty of ways to try to take advantage of the paths to the backfield: Burns, Abdul Carter, Kayvon Thibodeaux, Arvell Reese.

So while the Cowboys have dubbed themselves the "Greatest Offense There Is," the first test could be a tough one — especially if the Giants come up with a way to successfully attack the 40 percent of the offensive line about which the Cowboys should have real concerns.

"College GameDay" was in Austin for the showdown between the Texas Longhorns and Ohio State Buckeyes. "It's about us, don't listen to all that bulls—." 😭

Coach Saban isn't here for the Week 1 overreactions 🤣 pic.twitter.com/a7SiEikf6B

"I think all you guys need to calm down. I hear you've got rat poison over here for LSU by proclaiming that they're going to win the national championship after one game. We got people all over your alma mater Michigan about how they played last week. It's one game. I mean everybody has the opportunity to improve. It's a long season. title: Penn State's Koby Howard trying to buck trend of one-hit wonders at receiver
description: KeAndre Lambert-Smith and Harrison Wallace are among Nittany Lions receivers who've faltered after big season-opening outings in recent years.
fullText:
You wouldn't have known Penn State has had a problem at receiver by looking at Week 1 box scores from the recent past.

As encouraging as sophomore Koby Howard's monster performance in the Sept. 5 opener against Marshall was, he will need to demonstrate consistency in the coming weeks to prove that he can be the reliable and dynamic outside target this offense has sorely lacked as it's failed to perform in big games against peer programs like Ohio State, Notre Dame, Michigan and Oregon.

Howard hauled in six receptions for 161 yards and a touchdown against the Thundering Herd, leading the Nittany Lions to a 45-0 win at Beaver Stadium.

Required reading: Penn State's Matt Campbell embracing Joe Paterno's legacy in shift from predecessors

First-year coach Matt Campbell and offensive coordinator have drawn wide praise for their willingness to look downfield in the days since, with many fans seeing Howard's breakthrough effort as a stark departure from the conservatism that they feel characterized the final weeks for former coach James Franklin and OC Andy Kotelnicki. That assessment is largely ahistorical, though, and suffers from the same problem as recent years: A small sample size.

Receiver Keandre Lambert-Smith had a huge night in the 2023 opener against West Virginia. He caught four passes for 123 yards and two touchdowns in what was quarterback Drew Allar's first career start.

One year later, Harrison "Tre" Wallace III diced up the Mountaineers defense for five catches, 117 yards and two touchdowns of his own.

And last year, transfer receivers Trebor Pena (seven catches, 74 yards) and Kyron Hudson (six catches, 89 yards, one touchdown) had encouraging outings in their Penn State debuts against Nevada.

None of the four were able to sustain that success, especially once the Big Ten schedules began in earnest.

Lambert-Smith did not crack the 100-yard mark again for the rest of the season. He was held to six catches for 52 yards in a 20-12 loss at Ohio State. Then managed just one catch for six yards in a 24-15 home loss to Michigan that effectively eliminated Penn State from College Football Playoff consideration. He finished the season with 673 yards, so nearly 20% of his season production came in that first game.

Wallace similarly became ordinary through the Big Ten portion of Penn State's schedule. He surpassed the 60-yard threshold just twice over the rest of the season. He had just two catches in a 20-13 home loss to Ohio State; four catches for 59 yards in a Big Ten championship loss to Oregon; and no catches in the College Football Playoff semifinal loss to Notre Dame at the Orange Bowl that ended Penn State's bid to play for a title.

Hudson went on to become nearly a non-factor in 2025. He totaled 23 catches for 288 yards for the season. Pena was better, but no-showed in the back-to-back-to-back losses that got Franklin fired at midseason. He had two catches for 16 yards against Oregon, three catches for 15 yards against UCLA and two catches for five yards against Northwestern.

Howard has a different coach and different coordinator to help him avoid a similar fate, but that's the history he'll need to overcome.

"I think the sky is the limit for Koby Howard, and I'm really proud of him because, you were ready for this moment," Campbell said of the performance after the game. "You were ready when the opportunity came away, and I do think that is college football right here. Your shots come, the moment's going to come when you take advantage of it, and Koby's a guy that's worked so hard behind the scenes to take advantage of this moment, so I'm really happy for him."

The Pensacola, Fla., native's playing time was the subject of intense scrutiny after Franklin's firing in 2025.

A former three-star rated recruit by 247 Sports, many fans began to see him as a key piece of the program's future who should get opportunities over older transfer players like Hudson, Pena and Devonte Ross.

Instead, he played sparingly under interim coach Terry Smith. He finished the season with seven catches for 133 yards, all of them coming after Franklin's firing.

To his credit, Campbell, Mouser and quarterback Rocco Becht have shown early faith in him anyway. The question now is how far he can carry that forward. And Howard knows one game is far from an adequate answer.

"I feel like today was just a test, but you know it really doesn't stop here," he said after the game. "I've just got to keep proving myself and keep showing the coaches that they can trust me so that when those big moments come, they're ready to call my number."

title: Heads Dada wins, tails Ponting loses: When Sourav Ganguly pranked Australian captain at toss with 'head-tail' call
description: Clarke is not sure which match the incident took place in.
fullText:
Sourav Ganguly is widely regarded as one of the most influential captains in Indian cricket history. During his career, "Dada" was known for several memorable moments on and off the field, from making Steve Waugh wait at the toss and celebrating shirtless on the Lord's balcony to clashes with coaches Greg Chappell and John Buchanan, arguments with Shane Warne, and refusing to walk after Graeme Smith claimed a catch.

But former Australia captain Michael Clarke has shared another story that shows a lighter side of Ganguly.

In his book Eleven Gods and a Billion Indians, author Boria Majumdar quotes Clarke recalling an incident involving Ganguly and Ricky Ponting during a toss in India, although Clarke admits he does not remember which match it was.

"One of Clarke's favourite anecdotes goes thus: Ganguly and Ricky Ponting were out at the toss during one of the matches in India — Clarke doesn't specifically remember which one — and Ponting had the coin in hand. Just as he flipped the coin, Ganguly, if Clarke is to be believed, said, 'Head-Tail'.

"'Trust me, mate, that's what Ricky told me,' Clarke says, cracking up. 'Ricky said he couldn't fathom what had happened with Dada having said Head-Tail. [And, apparently it was said at the speed of lightning.] It had taken Ricky a second or two to come to grips with the situation and by that time the coin had come down. Ganguly just picked it up and said to Ricky, "We'll bat" and walked off. India had won the toss and were batting. Ricky did not really know what to do or say and all he did was tell us in the dressing room exactly what happened at the toss," Clarke was quoted as saying in the book.

Clarke is not sure which match the incident took place in.

According to available records, Ganguly won five tosses against Ricky Ponting, and all of those came outside India; twice during the 2003 World Cup and three times in the 2003-04 VB Series. That means Clarke may have mixed up the venue while recalling the story, as Ponting would have been the one calling the toss if the match had been played in India.

Clarke, however, clearly states that he does not remember the exact match in which the incident happened.

title: Brewers explode for 20 runs as playoff ticket becomes official
description: The Brewers are officially headed back to October after crushing the Reds 20-0, but Milwaukee has its sights set on a much bigger prize.
fullText:
Brewers explode for 20 runs as playoff ticket becomes official originally appeared on The Sporting News. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

The Milwaukee Brewers officially punched their ticket to October on Friday night, and they did it in emphatic fashion.

Milwaukee overwhelmed the Cincinnati Reds 20-0, using an unexpected power surge to secure its fourth consecutive postseason appearance and eighth playoff berth in the past nine seasons.

Garrett Mitchell delivered the biggest swing of the night, blasting Milwaukee's first grand slam of the season. The Brewers finished with four home runs, an impressive display for a club that entered Friday ranked last in Major League Baseball in homers.

The victory improved Milwaukee to 92-56 and guaranteed the team a spot in the postseason field. However, simply reaching October is no longer enough for a franchise that has become accustomed to playing meaningful baseball late in the year.

Manager Pat Murphy acknowledged the accomplishment with a clubhouse toast while making sure his players understood that bigger goals remain ahead.

"It's not something to take lightly because it's really hard to do," Murphy said. "We checked off one box, but we've got a lot more to go."

Milwaukee's next objective is securing the NL Central crown. The Brewers hold a commanding 10-game advantage over the Chicago Cubs, with their magic number sitting at four.

After that, attention will shift toward making a deeper postseason run.

The Brewers were swept by the Los Angeles Dodgers in last season's National League Championship Series, leaving unfinished business for a Milwaukee team hoping for another opportunity this October.

While home runs haven't defined the Brewers' offense, their ability to hit for average and reach base has helped make them one of baseball's most successful teams. Milwaukee also believes its starting rotation, led by Jacob Misiorowski, could become a major weapon during a postseason series.

Friday provided a chance to appreciate how far Milwaukee has come before turning its attention toward what comes next.

Mitchell summed up the moment perfectly.

"You have to celebrate the moment, no matter how big or small," Mitchell said.

For Milwaukee, the first celebration is complete.

Now comes the pursuit of something much bigger.

fullText:
Why Padres will clinch final NL Wild Card spot over Diamondbacks appeared first on ClutchPoints. 

The National League Wild Card race enters Saturday with a half-game gap between its final two serious contenders. The San Diego Padres stand at 79-68 and occupy the third Wild Card position. The Arizona Diamondbacks sit only half a game behind at 79-69. Despite that narrow margin, the Padres hold the far stronger path to October.

The Diamondbacks kept the pressure on the Padres Friday night by routing the Texas Rangers 9-1 for their fifth win in six games. However, San Diego answered with a 7-5 victory over the San Francisco Giants, extending its winning streak to five and preserving its half-game lead. The Padres have won seven of their last 10 and hold another important advantage with one additional game remaining.

San Diego has 15 games remaining in the season, beginning with two vs. the Giants and four vs. the Colorado Rockies. Those clubs enter Saturday with a combined record of 117-178. The Padres have an opportunity to create separation before facing another winning opponent.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

The Diamondbacks have 14 games remaining, beginning with the final two contests of their current series vs. the Rangers. Arizona will then host the Miami Marlins and New York Yankees, visit Colorado, and finish the season at Petco Park. The overall schedule remains manageable, but the three-game series vs. the Yankees represents a far tougher test than anything awaiting San Diego during its next six games.

The larger statistical picture also favors the Padres. San Diego owns a plus-19 run differential after scoring 626 runs and allowing 607. The Diamondbacks have produced more offense but carry only a plus-seven differential after surrendering 650 runs. That 43-run gap on the prevention side matters when every close September game can alter the standings.

The season series is tied 5-5, placing enormous importance on the final three meetings. Arizona visits Petco Park from September 25 to September 27, giving the Padres home-field advantage in a series that could determine both the final Wild Card berth and the head-to-head tiebreaker.

That setting favors the Padres. They are 46-29 at Petco Park, while the Diamondbacks must finish their season on the road. Playing those games at home should reduce travel strain and give the Padres an edge if the race reaches its final day. San Diego does face a difficult three-game trip against the Los Angeles Dodgers beforehand, but its softer upcoming stretch provides an opportunity to build a cushion.

The Diamondbacks are good enough to keep this race competitive until the final weekend. Their offense can erase deficits quickly, and Friday's rout showed how forcefully it can respond under pressure. Still, the Diamondbacks must overtake a hotter team with one fewer game to play.

The Padres control the schedule, own the better run differential, and host the decisive series. Those advantages will carry San Diego past Arizona and into the postseason with the National League's final Wild Card berth.

title: How can India qualify for the WTC final 2027? Qualification scenario, points and wins required to reach World Test Championship final
description: The Sporting News takes a look at the WTC 2027 Final qualification scenario for India.
fullText:
India's road to the ICC World Test Championship (WTC) Final 2027 has become much clearer following the recent Tests that were played.

As every match affects the percentage points table (PCT), India still finds themselves in the race, but with very little to spare as they move forward towards the end of the cycle.

In the first of the two Tests that India played against Sri Lanka, the visitors registered a massive 165-run victory in Galle and then aimed to complete a whitewash. However, a valiant performance from Sri Lanka in the final day of the 2nd Test in Colombo helped them to hold the visitors to a draw in the final match of the series.

After a surprise win over Australia in the first Test, Bangladesh succumbed to an embarrassing loss in the second and final match of the series in Mackay. Till date, Bangladesh hold on to the fourth position but India can overtake them if they win the second match.

England moved to the sixth position, replacing Sri Lanka after their 3-0 whitewash win over Pakistan on September 12.

In this article, The Sporting News takes an in-depth look at India's WTC 2027 Final Qualification scenario.

In one of their biggest challenges, the series-levelling effort in the English summer ensured that India started the WTC cycle 2025-27 on a good note. However, the wobble in the home series against South Africa have set them back significantly.

India are currently fifth on the WTC table, having won five of their 11 Test matches.

MORE: IND squad for SL Tests: Gill returns as captain for two-match series

Matches remaining for India: 7 Tests

Reaching the WTC Final is based on securing one of the top-two PCTs after the completion of the league stage. In the WTC rankings, the percentage of points is considered and not the number of points, so all Tests are equally important. Victory will earn them 12 points, while a draw earns four and a tie earns six.

Thus, India's qualification hopes will depend on maintaining a strong PCT for the rest of the WTC cycle. With an away tour to New Zealand now before a home series against Australia, every Test will be crucial.

India failed to capitalise on the away tour of Sri Lanka. While they won the series, they failed to complete a whitewash and remained fifth on the points table.

However, their prospects of securing themselves among the top two will also be contingent on the performance of the other teams.

The Oval in London will host the 2027 World Test Championship Final from June 9-13, 2027.

title: 4 reasons for optimism for Chargers against the Cardinals in Week 1
description: Here are four reasons to be optimistic about the Los Angeles Chargers starting out the season 1-0.
fullText:
The Chargers are set to kick off their 2026 season against the Arizona Cardinals on Sunday, giving fans their first real look at Mike McDaniel's offense and Chris O'Leary's defense under returning head coach Jim Harbaugh.

Here are four reasons to be optimistic about a win for Los Angeles.

All eyes will be on McDaniel and how he deploys quarterback Justin Herbert and running back Omarion Hampton on Sunday. The Chargers have already seen what the offense can look like in the preseason, where Herbert hit Quentin Johnston for a 65-yard touchdown on a deep shot, but getting a full game of McDaniel's scheme with Herbert under center will eclipse that excitement rather quickly. McDaniel has spoken highly of what Herbert's talents allow this offense to unlock, so watching for what a creative offensive mind like him has in store will be must-see TV.

Rashawn Slater and Joe Alt will start at offensive tackle for the first time since the 2024 Wild Card game, after Slater missed the 2025 season with a torn patellar tendon. Alt also missed all but six games with ankle injuries last season, sending the Chargers into desperation mode on the offensive line and allowing Herbert to be sacked 60 times, second-most in the NFL. Both bookends are now healthy, however, with fourth-round rookie Travis Burke standing out in the preseason and Trey Pipkins III returning as solid depth if necessary. Getting Slater and Alt back on the field - and Alt back to the right tackle spot where he was named a PFWA All-Rookie Team selection in 2024 - should give the Chargers even more freedom offensively.

Despite only playing 13 games, Cardinals starting quarterback Jacoby Brissett was sacked 43 times, sixth-most in the NFL and 7 more than Lamar Jackson, the next-most sacked quarterback who appeared in 13 games or fewer. Arizona responded this offseason by replacing Jonah Williams with Elijah Wilkinson at right tackle, but Wilkinson has been a borderline starter for most of his career and may not be a massive upgrade. With Khalil Mack, Tuli Tuipulotu, and first-round pick Akheem Mesidor rested up after minimal action in the preseason, Sunday could be rife with celebrations in the backfield if Arizona's 2025 tendencies continue into this season.

Cardinals rookie running back Jeremiyah Love suffered a high ankle sprain four weeks ago in a preseason game against the Raiders and only returned to practice this week in a limited fashion. Neither Love nor head coach Mike LaFleur has indicated whether Love will play Sunday or how limited he might be if he does, which could mean the Chargers avoid facing off against the 3rd overall pick from this April's draft. If Love is out, Arizona will start Tyler Allgeier with Bam Knight as the secondary back, while veteran James Conner is on injured reserve as well. With a bevy of other talented skill position players in Arizona, dodging Love this week may be a bit of a boost for the Chargers.

title: CBF mourns Paulo Angioni, Fluminense chief and 1990 Brazil aide
description: CBF mourns the passing of Paulo Angioni, Fluminense football director and Brazil National Team supervisor at the 1990 World Cup Credits: CBFThe Brazilian Football Confederation (CBF) deeply mourns the...
fullText:
CBF mourns the passing of Paulo Angioni, Fluminense football director and Brazil National Team supervisor at the 1990 World Cup Credits: CBF

The Brazilian Football Confederation (CBF) deeply mourns the passing this Saturday (12) of Paulo Angioni, Fluminense's executive football director and supervisor of the Brazilian National Team at the 1990 World Cup, and extends its condolences to the executive's family, friends, and fans. He was 80 years old and had been battling pancreatic cancer.

"Today we lost a pioneer, an executive who worked tirelessly for the professionalization and modernization of Brazilian football, always with great ethics and respect. Paulo Angioni leaves behind a legacy of dedication to football and appreciation for the human side of athletes, coaching staff, and club employees. In tribute to his victorious history, CBF will observe a minute of silence in all stadiums across Brazil this weekend," said CBF president Samir Xaud.

A native of Rio de Janeiro, born on June 5, 1946, the Rio-born executive had been active in football for four decades. He worked at several clubs in the country, including Palmeiras, Flamengo, Vasco, Bahia, Corinthians, and Olaria. At the time, he already served as football director, a position that would gain relevance and prominence over the years.

At Fluminense, the club he supported, he had four spells, the last beginning in 2018. During that period, he helped the club win a series of titles, including the 2022 and 2023 Rio de Janeiro State Championships, the 2023 CONMEBOL Libertadores, and the 2024 CONMEBOL Recopa.

In his role, Angioni was known and valued for building relationships of respect and care with the employees and athletes of the clubs he worked for. In its official statement, Fluminense highlighted this human side of the executive.

"His contribution to the development of young players will be remembered by many, and his lessons will remain with us as an example of life, compassion, and solidarity," the club wrote in its statement.

title: Why SEC is now 'not sure' it can take legal action vs LSU | Report
description: The latest update on the SEC's lawsuit against LSU as the eligibility crisis continues to rock college sports.
fullText:
The SEC's legal battle against Louisiana State remains at a standstill, and when the next move may happen seems to get farther and farther away.

ESPN college football insider Pete Thamel reported on "College GameDay" on Saturday, Sept. 12, that the SEC is "monitoring things right now" as "they're not sure they can take action against LSU because of that state court order in Louisiana."

Thamel did not go into specifics about the aforementioned state court order.

However, earlier this month, when East Baton Rouge Parish Judge William Jorden issued a preliminary injunction making it possible for LSU to roster players who had signed NFL contracts, the court order also barred the SEC from punishing LSU for playing those athletes.

The update comes after a federal hearing scheduled to take place at Hugo L. Black United States Courthouse in Birmingham on Wednesday, Sept. 9, was continued.

REQUIRED READING: Hearing in SEC suit against LSU postponed moments before Wednesday start

U.S. District Judge Annemarie Carney Axon was due to hear the SEC's request for a temporary restraining order against LSU, which was part of an amended complaint from the school, seeking protection against any retaliation that could result from decisions made during a specially-called meeting of SEC officials on Thursday, Sept. 10. Court filings described that the conference would vote on whether LSU should be expelled, but the conference shared a statement that afternoon indicating that the parties were working towards a resolution.

The scheduled 1 p.m. hearing was postponed and is expected to be rescheduled through a separate order. No reason for the delay was given.

The SEC filed suit against LSU on Thursday, Sept. 3, seeking preliminary and permanent injunctions tied to what it described as its First Amendment right of "expressive association" — in other words, the conference's argument that it cannot be forced to associate with a member acting contrary to its mission and values.

On the night before the scheduled Wednesday hearing, LSU rostered two other players to reach its 105-man roster limit, leaving no room for former NFL signees Dae'Quan Wright and Zxavian Harris.

Leading up to Sept. 9, Wright and Harris were granted preliminary injunctions allowing them to compete after initially receiving temporary restraining orders. The SEC argued that adding Wright and Harris would violate conference eligibility rules, and LSU's continued pursuit of their eligibility resulted in the conference's lawsuit.

The SEC filed an amended complaint on Tuesday, Sept. 8, seeking a temporary restraining order ahead of a Sept. 10 meeting of conference leaders, when LSU's membership in the league was expected to be considered, according to court filings.

In its filing, the SEC argued that having to associate with LSU would cause "irreparable harm" if the league were unable to distance its name, brand, championships and media properties from conduct it opposes.

Thamel's Saturday report indicates uncertainty over how the Louisiana court order continues to complicate what, if any, action the SEC can take against LSU while the federal case remains unresolved.

Emilee Smarr covers Alabama basketball and Crimson Tide athletics for The Tuscaloosa News. She can be reached via email at esmarr@usatodayco.com.

title: 🦁 Morgan Rogers joins iconic Chelsea pride with early opener against Hull
description: It's hard to argue that Morgan Rogers didn't make the right decision this summer when he opted to join Chelsea over their capital and Premier League rival Arsenal. His latest goal, a seventh-minute op...
fullText:
It's hard to argue that Morgan Rogers didn't make the right decision this summer when he opted to join Chelsea over their capital and Premier League rival Arsenal.

His latest goal, a seventh-minute opener against promoted Hull City, sees the England international midfielder continue his blistering start to life at Stamford Bridge.

After Chelsea broke into the attacking third through compatriot Cole Palmer, the Blues maestro picked out João Pedro, who turned to supply Rogers before the former Aston Villa man drove into the box and rifled low past Konstantinos Tzolakis to beat the Greek international shot-stopper at his near post.

With that, Rogers bagged his third goal of the early 2026/27 season and has now been credited with a direct goal contribution in each of Chelsea's opening four Premier League fixtures.

More impressively, Rogers has hallowed halls at the Bridge, too, now sitting alongside Didier Drogba, Cesc Fàbregas, Diego Costa, and Eden Hazard as just the fifth player to achieve that feat in that timeframe.

All told, Rogers has contributed a combined seven goals and assists in Chelsea's opening six fixtures in all competitions, already endearing himself to Blues supporters in all corners.

Though Arsenal already got the better of Chelsea in the league this season, Rogers surely won't mind if this run of form continues.

title: Rival watch: Atletico Madrid midfield ace a doubt for derby against Real Madrid
description: Real Madrid are in action later tonight as they take on Rayo Vallecano at the Santiago Bernabeu in La Liga.Once that is out of the way, the Merengues will tackle two matches over the next week in the ...
fullText:
Real Madrid are in action later tonight as they take on Rayo Vallecano at the Santiago Bernabeu in La Liga.

Once that is out of the way, the Merengues will tackle two matches over the next week in the league before the first international break of the new season arrives.

The first of the two fixtures will see Real Madrid take on Elche before facing local rivals Atletico Madrid away at the Riyadh Air Metropolitano – a game that Jose Mourinho & co. will have circled in red.

Now, leading up to the Madrileno derby, Atletico Madrid have been dealt a major injury blow.

Key midfielder Pablo Barrios suffered an injury during the Rojiblancos' UEFA Champions League clash with Liverpool, leaving his participation in next week's derby against Real Madrid in serious doubt, reports AS.

The news is a blow for Diego Simeone and a boost for Real Madrid with just over a week to go before the contest at the Metropolitano.

Atletico confirmed that Pablo Barrios has suffered a low-grade myofascial injury to his right leg.

The midfielder finished the Champions League meeting with Liverpool at Anfield experiencing discomfort, and subsequent medical tests confirmed the injury.

Barrios will definitely miss Sunday's La Liga match against Real Sociedad and is also expected to be unavailable for next week's fixture against Osasuna.

The bigger concern is the derby on 20 September, as Barrios faces a race against time to recover for the visit of Real Madrid.

Pablo Barrios is a major doubt to face Real Madrid. (Photo by Denis Doyle/Getty Images)

Atletico have not given a specific recovery timeline, stating only that his return will depend on how the injury develops. At present, however, the indications are not particularly encouraging.

Barrios' potential absence would be a significant setback for Simeone. The midfielder has established himself as an important part of Atletico Madrid's midfield.

Indeed, the 23-year-old Spaniard has started four out of Atleti's five matches across all competitions in 2026/27 so far, even registering an assist in the process.

As such, his absence could be felt dearly by the Colchoneros in the derby.

Simeone does have alternatives, including Koke, Morten Hjulmand, Johnny Cardoso, Rodrigo Mendoza and Obed Vargas, but replacing Barrios would still be a major challenge for one of the most important fixtures of the season.

title: Caleb Williams on importance of Bears setting the tone in Week 1
description: Chicago Bears quarterback Caleb Williams discusses the importance of setting the tone early against the Carolina Panthers.
fullText:
So far in Chicago Bears quarterback Caleb Williams' young career, he is 1-1 in season openers -- winning his first career NFL game in the 2024 opener and narrowly losing 27-24 to the Minnesota Vikings last year.

In neither of those seasons was the opener an indication of how the season would go. But, Williams and the Bears are looking to change that this year with a win in the opener and defending their NFC North title. It all starts with setting the tone early.

"I think [it's important] for all games and since this is our first one, it's the most important," Williams said. "Just being able to try and get out there, set the tone, start fast, get a couple completions, run the ball well early on, have great communication on the field and on the sideline. Staying level-headed I think is going to be a big piece of it, as a team and as a collective. Bad things are going to happen, but then the severity of the bad, we can sort of control.  In those moments, it's about being level-headed and controlling yourself and your attitude and your energy."

Chicago starts their season against the Carolina Panthers on Sunday. It will be the second time Williams has played against Carolina in his NFL career with the first time being in 2024 when the Bears won 36-10. In that game, he completed 69 percent of his passes for 304 passing yards and two touchdowns and was only sacked once.

This is a significantly better Panthers team than 2024, so the Bears probably will not win by 26 points. However, this is certainly a game they can walk away from with a win before playing their first NFC North game of the season against the Minnesota Vikings in Week 2.

title: GAME THREAD: Washington meets up with Kansas State
description: Good morning, Cougar football fans. Your Washington State Cougars are getting ready for Week 2 non-conference action against the Kansas State Wildcats. WSU is coming off a narrow loss at rival Washington on Sunday, 24-10. Despite the loss, the Cougars had plenty of positives to take away from the Apple Cup. Mainly, from the defensive […]
fullText:
Good morning, Cougar football fans.

Your Washington State Cougars are getting ready for Week 2 non-conference action against the Kansas State Wildcats.

WSU is coming off a narrow loss at rival Washington on Sunday, 24-10. Despite the loss, the Cougars had plenty of positives to take away from the Apple Cup. Mainly, from the defensive side of things. The Cougar defense held Washington to just 10 points through the first three quarters and 2-10 on third-down conversions. It wasn't until Washington's final two drives that they really began to stack up the yards and explosive plays. In a game that WSU was three-possession underdogs in, they were within a score at multiple points in the final quarter. The front seven is what stood out for WSU in that game, containing the Huskies' run attack and putting pressure on quarterback Demond Williams Jr. Offensively, the Cougars have room for improvement. They will likely be without speedster wide receiver Tony Freeman, who suffered an injury in Week 1. Caden Pinnick showed flashes of brilliance last time out, scampering for 61 yards and a touchdown, and seemed to settle in later in the game with his arm.

Kansas State cruised through Week 1, defeating FCS Nicholls State 71-3. Quarterback Avery Johnson threw for 199 yards and three touchdowns before coming out of the game midway through the third quarter. Six different Wildcats ran in touchdowns in the game, with junior Rodney Fields Jr. leading the way with 101 yards on 14 carries and one of those six touchdowns.

Kickoff is set for 9 a.m. PST and will be broadcasted nationally on TNT and streaming on HBO Max.

title: Arsenal Starting XI vs Sunderland: Confirmed Team News and Predicted Lineup
description: Arsenal Team News: Bruno Guimaraes in Line for Sunderland StartArsenal may finally hand Bruno Guimaraes his first Premier League start when they travel to Sunderland on Saturday night. Mikel Arteta ha...
fullText:
Arsenal may finally hand Bruno Guimaraes his first Premier League start when they travel to Sunderland on Saturday night. Mikel Arteta has taken his time with the £75million summer signing, largely because of minor injury issues, but the signs now point towards a proper introduction.

Guimaraes came off the bench against Napoli in midweek and looks ready for a bigger role. The expectation is that he could start next to Declan Rice, which would give Arsenal more control in midfield and a bit more steel in a game that could get noisy quickly. His Newcastle past guarantees a hostile reception at the Stadium of Light, but managers do not pick teams based on crowd sentiment.

Arteta is also expected to freshen up the side after the 1-0 win in Naples. Christos Tzolis and Kai Havertz should return to the starting XI after limited minutes in Europe, while Riccardo Calafiori is tipped to come back in at left-back in place of Piero Hincapie.

There are also decisions to make around fitness. Ben White is available despite going off late against Napoli, while Jurrien Timber and Cristhian Mosquera are both pushing for squad involvement. Timber, in particular, is edging closer after a long spell out.

Arteta said: "Let's see, we have another training session [on Friday]," and added, "He's been doing really well, he's been training with us now for a few days and he looks in good shape."

Mosquera appears less likely to feature, but he is not far away. Arteta said: "He's been doing really well," before adding, "Let's see if he can get this game or the next one. It will be around that time, I think."

One absentee is certain. William Saliba remains out for an extended period after aggravating a back problem while on France duty earlier this summer. He avoided surgery, which matters, but Arsenal still have to manage without one of their most important defenders.

Predicted Arsenal XI, 4-2-3-1: Raya, White, Konsa, Gabriel, Calafiori, Rice, Guimaraes, Saka, Odegaard, Tzolis, Havertz.

Kick-off is 8pm BST on Saturday, September 12, 2026, at the Stadium of Light. On paper, Arsenal have more quality. The real point of interest is whether Guimaraes now becomes part of the core rather than an expensive option from the bench.

title: Vincent Kompany discusses Luis Díaz’s poor form as of late
description: The Columbian forward has struggled to convert his chances this season.
fullText:
Bayern Munich's start to the season has left fans with little to complain about, but winger Luis Díaz has struggled to find the back of the net as often as he is usually capable of. Díaz has scored just once while accumulating 3.79 xG this season, and the drop in form has become noticeable enough to draw Vincent Kompany's attention.

When asked about it as Bayern prepare themselves to face SV Elversberg in the Bundesliga this weekend, Kompany said: "[Díaz] just lacks the finishing touch. His energy is there, and he's a constant threat. You also have to get into those positions first, keep making those runs in behind. At the moment, he's getting into those situations and maybe lacking a bit of luck at the end – the shot is deflected, or another player sticks a foot in. But the important thing is that he's getting the chances and he needs to stay calm; then he'll be successful in front of goal again."

While fans have suggested this could stem from fatigue, Kompany sees no cause to worry. Regardless, fans are sure to hope that Díaz returns to form sooner rather than later.
