title: Cam Schlittler’s not the AL MVP … right?
description: Haha JK … unless?
fullText:
Regular readers know that I've followed one of the great Cy Young horse races in recent memory, with Cam Schlittler going great start-for-great start with the Blue Jays' Dylan Cease. We got a little bit of separation this week, as the Athletics touched up Cease for four runs in five innings on Monday, and then Schlittler allowed just a solo shot in seven frames against the Rockies on Tuesday. Cam has crept just ahead by fWAR, enjoys a considerable lead in bWAR, and right now I think would end up at the top of most voters' ballots.

But something struck me in the aftermath of Cam's night against Colorado, the same night that Aaron Judge returned to the lineup. Cam Schlittler isn't just the Cy Young favorite, but he's built himself an MVP case. No pitcher has won the award since Clayton Kershaw for the 2014 Dodgers, and the last AL winner was 2011 Justin Verlander. Yordan Alvarez is in the hunt for the first Triple Crown since Miguel Cabrera, Bobby Witt Jr. is probably the best overall player in the league, and if Junior Caminero tops the AL in home runs and plays on the Junior Circuit's best team, he probably gets his share of votes too.

And yet here's the thing: Cam stacks up fairly against all three of them!

Let's take Yordan, who I think has the inside track on the award right now. Schlittler's 0.1 fWAR back, a difference that is literally negligible, and more than three-quarters of a win better by bWAR. Alvarez's candidacy is based around the Triple Crown, probably being the best hitter in baseball, and dragging what we thought was a finally-deflated Houston Astros team to a division title. Crappy AL West or not, that is exactly the blueprint for an MVP, if one for a slightly older voter.

Should Alvarez not win the Triple Crown, he loses a bit of his case, though he's likely still the best hitter in the game on a division winner, one who will have played in the neighborhood of 155 games. That's the big thing both undercutting Witt's MVP claim while bolstering his position as best all-around player — the Kansas City shortstop has only played 128 games at time of writing, yet leads the league in fWAR and bWAR among position players. With a solid-but-not-spectacular 18 homers and 124 wRC+, the parts of his game beyond hitting are doing the heavy lifting there as well. All that and the fact that the Royals are so bad work against him when it comes to end of season awards though, and Bobby seems cursed to be the Dave Stieb of shortstops.

Junior Caminero, fittingly, is the junior candidate in this slate, trailing the rest of the field pretty clearly by WAR. The home run totals (an AL-leading 39 as of the time of writing) and the Rays' season of devil magic help fill in some of the gaps that would otherwise leave him a downballot vote-getter that helped a lot of people's fantasy teams, and in the end he might be just that. Great season, frightening player, but more of a top-five finisher than taking home the hardware.

Cam Schlittler leads the entire AL in bWAR, position players or no. He is virtually tied for third in fWAR. Perhaps most key to his case is the way this Yankee team has been beaten up, with four of his fellow starters seeing IL time this year. The Yankees came into the season with more starting pitching than they needed, and it ended up being just enough, with a chunk of that being because Schlittler has been so reliable, not missing a single start. Virtually every member of the regular starting lineup, save Ben Rice and Paul Goldschmidt, has been injured or demoted in some form this year, and the Opening Day center fielder, DH, and second baseman might not even finish the season on the big-league roster.

Through all that, the consistent, balancing force has been Cam's right arm every five days.

MVPs are built on a combination of statistical success and compelling narrative — Aaron Judge's 2022 was at that point his career-best season, but the chase for 62 is what pushed him over the line. Cam has the total value arguments, and certainly if you can make a compelling case for MVP you have to be the favorite for the Cy Young. Moreover, him being at 25 the stabilizing energy for a team that could very well have completely fallen apart, he may end up higher than you think on the ballot that means the most.

title: Manon Fiorot vs. Alexa Grasso prediction, pick, time for Noche UFC
description: Manon Fiorot says she's been told a win over Alexa Grasso at Noche UFC will get her another flyweight title shot. Can ex-champ Grasso play spoiler?
fullText:
Manon Fiorot and Alexa Grasso meet at Noche UFC on Saturday at Diamond Desert Arena in Glendale, Ariz. Check out this quick breakdown of the matchup from MMA Junkie analyst Dan Tom.

After her flyweight title loss to champ Valentina Shevchenko, Manon Fiorot (13-2 MMA, 8-1 UFC) got back in the win column in May with a quick knockout of Jasmine Jasudavicius. It was the fastest win of her career, just her second first-round win, and her first stoppage since 2021.

Alexa Grasso (17-5-1 MMA, 9-5-1 UFC) had consecutive losses to Valentina Shevchenko, in which she lost the flyweight title, and upcoming vacant title challenger Natalia Silva. But she bounced back in March in a big way with a $100,000 bonus-winning knockout of Maycee Barber in Seattle.

Serving as a solid showdown between top-tier women's flyweights, former title challenger Manon Fiorot will meet former champion Alexa Grasso.

Both women are coming off spectacular finishes in their last fights, particularly Grasso. In fact, Grasso's finishes over both Maycee Barber and Valentina Shevchenko lay out a potential blueprint for how she could succeed against a southpaw like Fiorot.

As I said in my breakdown ahead of Fiorot's title fight with Shevchenko, I correctly suspected that the Frenchwoman struggled with facing a fellow southpaw. No one hates fighting southpaw more than other southpaws.

Seemingly understanding this, Grasso has mixed in a healthy amount of southpaw looks against the previously mentioned lefties to great success. The problem, however, is that a lack of output urgency and corralling footwork has made Grasso a hard fighter to confidently back from a consistency standpoint (hence standing at 1-2-1 against UFC-level southpaws despite having avenues for success in every fight).

Grasso may be but a dynamic moment away from shifting this fight's trajectory, but I'll officially pick the larger and more consistent fighter in Fiorot to edge out a decision on the scorecards.

The oddsmakers and the public favor the French fighter, listing Fiorot -245 and Grasso +200 via FanDuel.

Fiorot and Grasso are expected to walk to the cage at approximately 6:15 p.m. ET. The fight streams live on Paramount+.

title: 3 reasons to hate Cowboys' matchup vs Giants starts with coaching
description: A new head coach and a lethal pass rush are a few of the reasons to hate the Dallas Cowboys' Week 1 matchup with the New York Giants.
fullText:
Another season begins with the Dallas Cowboys and New York Giants battling each other to start 1-0 in the NFC East race. Lately it's been the Cowboys getting the wins, especially when Dak Prescott is under center.

Things have a way of getting turned around when it comes to rivalries. Despite the Cowboys owning the matchups in the last 10 years, the Giants could be primed to make things more difficult. New York has made some significant changes this offseason that will challenge the Cowboys.

Here are three reasons to hate playing the Giants on Sunday night football to open the season.

Despite dominating the games between the two teams recently, the Cowboys need to be wary of a Giants team that's turned over their franchise to a Super Bowl winning coach. John Harbaugh arrives with a winning pedigree and a 4-1 record against the Cowboys, who have been feasting on poor coaches in New York since Tom Coughlin left.

The Giants' culture has changed with Harbaugh's arrival, and the first matchup with a new regime always brings surprises. Harbaugh's a veteran coach, but he hired Matt Nagy as his offensive coordinator, with whom he's never worked with as his OC, and Dennard Wilson is a first-time defensive coordinator. That can make for the Cowboys seeing some things they haven't seen from the Giants on both sides of the ball.

The Cowboys have a new coordinator, new scheme and new players on their defense, all in an effort to end the misery of not being able to stop the run. They'll face their first challenge in Skattebo and Giants' new rushing attack.

Skattebo isn't a top running back in the league yet, but he is a physical runner who's focused on punishing the Dallas defense.

Kay Adams: 

“First carry against the Cowboys, you tell me what that’s going to feel like.”

Cam Skattebo:

“It’s going to be punishment to the defense.”

(Via: @heykayadams) pic.twitter.com/Oz5kke7j3L

The second-year RB had a strong start to his career, averaging over four yards a carry and scoring seven touchdowns in his first eight games before a gruesome ankle injury ended his rookie season. If he continues down that path and has gotten better behind an improved line that includes 10th overall selection Francis Mauigoa, the Cowboys will have their hands full slowing down the run.

It'll be a big test for Christian Parker and the Cowboys' new look defense.

The Giants haven't been doing many things well on defense, but they have excelled at getting after the quarterback with their stable of pass rushers. Led by veteran edge rusher Brian Burns, the Giants can bring pressure with a strong group of four.

Burns was second in the NFL last season with 16.5 sacks and had 22 tackles for a loss. He's paired up with pass rusher Abdul Carter, who's looking to make a significant second-year jump. Carter had just four sacks but a high number of pressures as a rookie, which could turn into more sacks this season.

The defense also has former top-five pick Kayvon Thibodeaux and this year's fifth pick, Arvell Reese, to make life difficult for Prescott. Thibodeaux has 23.5 career sacks and Reese is coming off an All-American 2025 campaign where he had 10 sacks.

It's a scary group of pass rushers to begin with, and when coupled with guard Tyler Smith's absence, it could make things much tougher on the Cowboys' offense.

title: India vs Sri Lanka Women’s Asia Cup final: Start time, TV channel and live streaming details for IND-W vs SL-W
description: Defending champions Sri Lanka are all set to defend their crown against last edition's runner-up, India, and here's where you can catch the game live
fullText:
India vs Sri Lanka Women's Asia Cup final: Start time, TV channel and live streaming details for IND-W vs SL-W originally appeared on Cricket News. Add Cricket News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

India will face Sri Lanka in the final of the 2026 Women's Asia Cup on Sunday.

The two sides faced each other in the 2024 finals as well, with Sri Lanka emerging as the winners.

This will be India's sixth consecutive finals since the tournament shifted to the T20 format.

After a thrilling semifinal that saw Sri Lanka W's win their game against Pakistan by the narrowest of margins, the finals of the 2026 Women's Asia Cup are all set for a repeat of 2024. Only this time, it will be Sri Lanka entering the final match as the defending champions.

But the win did not come easily. Sri Lanka were nearly undone after getting reduced to 33 for 4 to chase down Pakistan's 130 for 5 with eight balls to spare in the second semi-final, with Fatima Sana's unbeaten 47 and 4 for 36 going in vain for the Pakistan captain.

Nilakshika Silva and Kaushini Nuthyangana saw Sri Lanka home after a 67-run stand from Harshitha Samarawickrama and Kavisha Dilhari had done the heavy lifting earlier in the chase.

Meanwhile, India remains the favourite as they cruised through the group stage before making short work of Bangladesh in the semis. Shafali Verma made a blistering 64 off 40 to take India to 149 for 5 before Deepti Sharma took three wickets to wrap up Bangladesh for 109.

With this, Harmanpreet Kaur's side have reached their sixth consecutive finals since the tournament was shifted from the 50-over to 20-over format. It will also be India's chance to avenge their loss from 2024.

Set for Sunday, September 13, at the Dubai International Cricket Stadium, both sides arrive unbeaten through the knockout stage, with one having all the momentum on their side.

MORE: 'His time will come': Rahane wants India to drop Sooryavanshi to accommodate Samson

India go into the final as the form side of the tournament, unbeaten since their defeat against the Aussies in June and carrying momentum from Verma's player-of-the-match display in the semi-final. Sharma's control through the middle overs has been central to India's bowling, while Smriti Mandhana's earlier century against Hong Kong underlined the depth of India's top order.

Sri Lanka, however, has made a habit of peaking at exactly the right moment against the bigger sides in this tournament. Chamari Athapaththu's all-round influence and a batting order capable of recovering from genuine trouble, as shown against both Bangladesh and Pakistan in the knockouts, make them a side few teams will want to face with a title on the line.

Given the history between these two sides in Asia Cup finals and Sri Lanka's recent record of peaking at the knockout stage, India will know this rematch carries considerably more weight than a routine group-stage formality.

The final will be played on Sunday, September 13, at the Dubai International Cricket Stadium.

title: Dallas Cowboys draft: College football’s top targets in Week 2
description: Do you have any favorite draft prospects already?
fullText:
It's never too early to start thinking about potential draft picks of the Dallas Cowboys in the future. Here are some prospects that could be interesting who are playing this weekend.

This is the main event of Week 2 and features two players likely to be selected near the beginning of the 2027 NFL Draft. Ohio State and Texas both won comfortably in their opening games, but this matchup will provide a much stronger test.

The 6-foot-3, 223-pound junior produced 87 receptions for 1,243 yards and 12 touchdowns last season, taking his career total to 2,558 yards and 27 scores in only two years.

His size, speed and body control make him extremely difficult to cover one-on-one. Smith can run away from defensive backs, win contested catches and adjust to passes thrown outside his frame. He is especially dangerous after the catch because he has the strength to run through contact without losing his speed.

The challenge against Texas will show how Smith handles physical coverage and extra defensive attention. The Longhorns will know where he is on every snap, so his ability to create separation when the defense is designed to stop him will be important.

George Pickens is playing under the franchise tag, and Dallas has not given him a long-term contract. That leaves his future beyond this season uncertain. Smith could eventually give the Cowboys another dominant receiver alongside CeeDee Lamb and allow the offense to remain aggressive through the air.

Smith is expected to be selected very early, meaning Dallas might need to move up to get him.

Simmons has 21 sacks, 29.5 tackles for loss and six forced fumbles already on his college record, and he finished 2025 with 12 sacks and earned first-team All-SEC honours.

His first-step speed is his greatest weapon. Simmons can explode past an offensive tackle before the blocker has properly settled into position. He can also bend around the corner while maintaining his balance and closing quickly on the quarterback.

This game gives Simmons an opportunity to face an Ohio State offensive line filled with NFL-level talent. Scouts will want to see whether he can still create pressure when an opponent slides protection toward him.

Dallas added Rashan Gary to start opposite Donovan Ezeiruaku, but a team can never have too many pass rushers, even with rookie addition Malachi Lawrence. Simmons would bring the burst and natural finishing ability needed to become a major part of the Cowboys' defensive front.

Gary is an established veteran, while Simmons could give Dallas a younger and cheaper long-term option on the edge while Lawrence continues to develop in his second year.

Oklahoma travels to Ann Arbor to face a Michigan team that narrowly escaped with a 13-12 victory over Western Michigan last week. This game features a powerful defensive tackle and a productive running back who could address future needs in Dallas.

Stone is a 6-foot-3, 315-pound defensive tackle with an impressive combination of strength and quickness. He can hold his position against double-team blocks, but he is also athletic enough to attack the gap between two offensive linemen.

His hands are powerful, allowing him to knock blockers backwards or remove their grip before moving toward the ball. Stone is still developing his pass-rush plan, but his ability to collapse the middle of the pocket can prevent quarterbacks from stepping forward to avoid outside pressure.

Stone could become the next powerful interior defender the Cowboys use in their three-man front. His size would help protect the linebackers against the run, while his quickness could provide pressure directly in front of the quarterback. That ability to affect both the running and passing games would make him a valuable early-round target and makes an already strong front even more formidable.

Marshall rushed for 932 yards and ten touchdowns in 2025 despite playing in only 11 games. He averaged 6.2 yards per carry and showed that he can handle contact without losing his ability to produce explosive runs.

Marshall has the build to run between the tackles. He reads his blocks patiently, makes one cut and then accelerates into open space. He is also willing to finish runs by lowering his shoulder rather than constantly trying to escape toward the sideline.

Dallas re-signed Javonte Williams, but the team still needs to consider the long-term future of the position. Jaydon Blue has gone, while Malik Davis is better suited to a supporting role which he will prove this year how well he can handle that role (depending on his injury).

Marshall could provide a physical option who keeps the offense on schedule and helps Dallas control games. He would not need to carry the entire workload immediately, making him a possible second-day selection who could begin in a rotation before earning a larger role.

title: 'I've turned the page' - Camara on Chelsea deal collapse
description: Monaco and Senegal midfielder Lamine Camara says he is moving on from his failed £47.1m move to Chelsea.
fullText:
Monaco midfielder Lamine Camara says he has "turned the page" and is focusing on the Ligue 1 season after his £47.1m move to Chelsea collapsed.

The 22-year-old had completed a medical but the deal fell through shortly before the transfer window closed.

Two bids had already been rejected, but Monaco lowered their asking price in a turbulent end to the window when it looked likely that Folarin Balogun's move to Everton was in doubt.

When Balogun's transfer appeared to be back on track, Monaco appeared to change their decision to sell Camara, but in the end both players stayed with the Ligue 1 side.

"There was a possibility I could leave," Camara said, speaking before Monaco's game against Strasbourg on Saturday.

"It didn't go through at the last minute and that's part of football. I've turned the page and am focusing on the season."

Sources in France had stated Monaco needed to make a major sale this summer and preferred to sell Balogun. A source at the Ligue 1 club had previously indicated it would take a "substantial fee" to secure Camara's departure.

Monaco have won their first three Ligue 1 fixtures of the season and sat second to Rennes in the table, with a game in hand, heading into the weekend.

"I can help the team a lot," Senegal international Camara said.

"Football moves fast. Maybe other opportunities will come along. But for now, I'm staying focused on the season with Monaco."

title: 11-year-old girl arrested on murder charge in 15-year-old brother's killing
description: Oklahoma police arrested an 11-year-old girl on a second-degree murder charge after her 15-year-old brother was fatally shot.
fullText:
Police in Oklahoma have arrested an 11-year-old girl on a murder charge after they say she fatally shot her older brother.

The Edmond Police Department, in a post on social media, reported that the shooting involved the girl's 15-year-old brother and took place on Sept. 9.

Officers were notified of a shooting in a residential area about 4 p.m. CT that day, The Oklahoman, part of the USA TODAY Network, reported, and when police arrived, found the teenage boy dead.

The area is about 15 miles north of downtown Oklahoma City.

Just before 1 a.m. the next day, police said, investigators arrested the victim's sister and transported her to a juvenile detention facility, where she was booked on a second-degree murder charge.

A motive in the shooting has not been released by police or the Oklahoma County District Attorney's Office, which will ultimately determine whether to prosecute the case.

"We recognize this is a heartbreaking situation for the family involved," Edmond police said. "Our thoughts are with them as they grieve this tragedy."

Because the case involves juveniles, no additional information had been released by police about the fatal shooting as of Sept. 11.

The District Attorney's Office, in a post on social media, said Oklahoma state law limits what information can be shared about the case due to the ages of the suspect and reported victim.

USA TODAY does not identify minor suspects in juvenile cases unless they are officially charged and prosecuted as adults.

Natalie Neysa Alund is a senior reporter for USA TODAY. Reach her at nalund@usatoday.com and follow her on X @nataliealund.

title: Pennsylvania lawmaker suggests Trump should rename Lake Erie to 'Lake Pennsylvania'
description: Pennsylvania state Rep. David Maloney wants President Donald Trump to rename Lake Erie to "Lake Pennsylvania," following recent name changes to other bodies of water.
fullText:
Pennsylvania state Rep. David Maloney, a Republican, is asking President Donald Trump to rename Lake Erie to "Lake Pennsylvania" following similar renaming efforts by the president.

Maloney is preparing a resolution calling on Trump, Interior Secretary Doug Burgum and lawmakers on Capitol Hill to take steps to rename Lake Erie to "Lake Pennsylvania," arguing that the change is needed to reflect the lake's modern identity.

"This is Pennsylvania's only Great Lake. Its modern economy and identity are increasingly tied to the boaters, anglers, families and tourists who come to enjoy it," Maloney said in a statement. "Ohio has plenty of shoreline. New York already has two Great Lakes. Canada has four others."

New York Gov Hochul Rejects Trump's 'Lake America' Renaming With Blunt Message

"Pennsylvania has one. Let's call it Lake Pennsylvania!" he added.

Lake Erie is the smallest of the Great Lakes by volume as well as the shallowest, according to the Environmental Protection Agency. The lake has about 12 million people in its watershed, with 10.5 million people in the U.S. and 1.9 million people in Canada.

This comes after Trump signed an executive order last month to rename Lake Ontario to "Lake America," a rebranding that Canada does not recognize and has firmly rejected.

"We know that America is changing. Their trading relationships, their foreign policies, their national monuments, their hydronyms. Canadians also know that naming reality means calling it Lake Ontario — then, now and always," Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said in a statement.

South Park Creators Mock Trump's Lake Ontario Rename And Company Compliance In Mock Statement

The renaming only applies to the U.S. federal government, meaning Canada, other international bodies and U.S. states are not forced to acknowledge the change. But both Apple Maps and Google Maps changed the name of Lake Ontario to "Lake America" for U.S. users following Trump's executive order.

The president has also suggested renaming New Mexico to "New America," prompting several of the state's Democratic lawmakers to call on Apple and Google to publicly commit to keeping the state's current name on their respective maps applications.

Trump has also floated the idea of renaming the Pacific and Atlantic Oceans.

On his first day back in office in January 2025, Trump signed an executive order to rename the Gulf of Mexico to the "Gulf of America," but, similar to the Lake Ontario rebranding, the order only applies to the U.S. federal government and does not bind Mexico, other international bodies or private entities.

Apple Maps and Google Maps also adopted this change for users in the U.S., implementing the update using a region-based approach tailored to the location of the user's device.

title: United Airlines CEO says he sleeps 8 ½ hours a night and limits meetings to 'no more than 4 hours a day’
description: United Airlines CEO Scott Kirby says that being protective of his schedule gives him more time to think, read, and sleep.
fullText:
United Airlines CEO Scott Kirby doesn't have time for endless meetings.

Instead, he sleeps eight and a half hours a day and reads roughly 2 books a week.

Does his advice change how you would structure your day?

Don't think that United Airlines CEO Scott Kirby is going to sit through your slide deck.

"If you want to send a deck, send it to me in advance, and then we're just going to talk about it, but you're not going to read slides to me," Kirby told Semafor's "CEO Signal" podcast.

Kirby is fiercely protective of his schedule. That's why he caps meetings at four hours per day, though he said he averages less. It means keeping the meetings he does have quick and conversational.

"That gives me time to think," he said. "The further you go in your career, certainly by the time you're the CEO, your job is not to work hard. It's to think hard."

In Kirby's schedule, "Sleep is the number one priority." He said he gets eight and a half hours a night. He also has a rotating set of four workouts, but if he's traveling and his schedule is compressed, it's sleep that remains the key.

The United CEO said he wakes up at 5:30 am. He doesn't need an alarm. He'll look at emails, but "that's like five minutes."

As for the rest of the day, Kirby said he devotes three hours to reading.

"I read The Wall Street Journal cover to cover and probably 15 minutes worth of The New York Times," he said. "Reading cover to cover, I find all kinds of interesting stuff that I would've never known if I wouldn't have searched for it."

Most afternoons, Kirby will also squeeze in a 15-to 20-minute nap.

On top of that, Kirby said he has five magazines he'll look through, depending on when they arrive. He also said he reads about two books a week. His favorite genre is science fiction.

"But it's really hard to find good science fiction," he said. "Isaac Asimov is my favorite. The best science fiction I've read in the last 20 years was probably 'The Three-Body Problem.'"

In a 2025 interview, Kirby detailed some of the things he cuts from his life to save time for what matters.

"I just naturally don't want to waste time," Kirby told former Fast Company editor-in-chief Bob Safian during an interview for Safian's "Rapid Response" podcast. "I'm not on social media. What a colossal waste of time on social media. I don't do that. I don't watch TV."

Kirby, who has seven kids, said when he's at home, he puts them to bed and takes them to school anytime he can.

"So, lots of sleep, lots of time with the family," Kirby told Safian.

All of it comes back to what Kirby sees as the scourge of careers: meetings.

"One of the best things people can do for their careers, I think, is stop with all the madness of meetings," he said.

Without all those meetings, people have time for what they actually need.

"You need time to think, to come up with ideas, to be creative, to walk around, to talk to other people," he said, "and you can't do it if you're sitting in meetings all day."

If you enjoyed this story, be sure to follow Business Insider on Yahoo.

title: Who has given selectors food for thought? England-Pakistan player ratings
description: Which batter played his most mature innings of the year? Who has given the selectors food for thought? Player ratings from England's win over Pakistan at Edgbaston.
fullText:
England have wrapped up victory over Pakistan in the third Test by eight wickets to seal a 3-0 series win.

Here's how the players rated at Edgbaston.

Emilio Gay - 6 - A gritty Test-best of 60 in tricky batting conditions in the first innings looked to have gone some way towards securing his place on the plane for a winter tour of South Africa, only for a duck next time round to bring back some uncertainty. (Series - 6)

Ben Duckett - 2 - A miserable end to the summer for the opener who will now come under some scrutiny. Made 11 and zero in this match and finishes this three-Test series well down the averages with a disappointing 44 runs at 8.8. (Series - 2)

Jordan Cox - 7 - A cheap dismissal in the first innings but made a nerveless unbeaten 59 to take the sting out of Pakistan after a wobble in the chase. A particularly impressive effort with the gloves - taking five dismissals - after being called upon to keep following Jamie Smith's injury may have given the selectors food for thought in the role. (Series - 7)

Joe Root - 7 - Question marks over his captaincy during Pakistan's second innings, but got England over the line with 62 not out. A 10th lbw in 14 innings suggests a technical issue which still needs to be ironed out by England's all-time leading run-scorer. (Series - 7)

Harry Brook - 7 - Batted with real discipline and focus at a time when Pakistan had a foothold in the game on day one. His most mature Test knock this year. Ran himself out on 75 when a century beckoned but forgivable given the application he showed earlier. Finishes as leading run-scorer in the series with 215 runs at 53.75. (Series - 8)

Dan Lawrence - 7 - Having been shunted around the order the Surrey all-rounder batted with the kind of confidence to suggest he might deserve a sustained run in the middle during a measured 65. Bowling underused but a not-too-shabby batting average of 46.75 will help his winter touring prospects. (Series - 7)

Jamie Smith - 6 - Not quite back to his fluent best but will be satisfied to notch up useful half-centuries in consecutive Tests. Kept reasonably well in Pakistan's first innings before a finger injury kept him off the field in the second. (Series - 6)

Gus Atkinson - 6 - Wicketless in the first innings and it initially looked like it was going to be another hard-luck tale. However, he shook off the weariness and a change to the City End allowed him to pocket three wickets to lighten his mood. (Series - 5)

Jofra Archer - 7 - Took a bit of tap in the second innings but bowled with plenty of zip and aggression throughout. A brutal ball to dismiss Saud Shakeel was a reminder of his menace. England will be desperate to keep him fit and firing during a pivotal 12 months. (Series - 8)

Ollie Robinson - 8 - Is there anyone better with a Dukes ball in English conditions? Another masterclass in control. England's tone-setter finishes the series with 21 wickets at a miserly 8.76. A breezy half-century on day two also entertained the crowd. (Series - 9)

Josh Tongue - 7 - Mopped up the tourists' lower order in the first innings with 4-42. Healthy returns in all three Tests - 19 wickets in all - and continues to look a vital cog in the machine. (Series - 8)

Azan Awais - 7 - Still finding his feet at Test level. Made a battling 59 off 84 balls in the second innings, after Pakistan were reduced to 0-2, and looks a player worth persisting with.

Saim Ayub - 1 - Called up for this Test after wholesale changes to the Pakistan side and looked drastically undercooked having not played a first-class fixture since October last year. Almost inevitably he bagged a pair. Scrapes a point for leaving the CPL at the drop of a hat to turn up.

Abdullah Shafique - 1 - Two half-centuries in the series but under leaden skies he was easy meat for Robinson and snared by the Sussex slayer for three and nought.

Shan Masood - 8 - A tame dismissal in the first innings but rolled up his sleeves second time around as he manufactured a composed and defiant 95 to top score for the tourists.

Babar Azam - 6 - Provided a reminder that with bat in hand, on his day, he is up there with the best players in the world to watch. A classy 76 was too little, too late, and as a polarising figure in Pakistan cricket might feel the heat in his role as captain.

Saud Shakeel - 6 - Rode his luck on occasions as he top-scored in the first innings with 43 then made 29 before being on the end of rasping bouncer from Archer. Finished Pakistan's leading run-scorer in the series with 204 at 34.00.

Ghazi Ghori - 2 - A largely unremarkable debut with the bat - scores of four and 16 - and struggled keeping wicket when he had to stand up to the stumps for large periods, leaking 18 byes.

Mohammad Imran - 6 - The most economical of Pakistan's bowlers who brought some vital control to curtail England's free scoring.

Razaullah Khan - 9 - A star is born. The 21-year-old brought a bit of bite to the Pakistan attack and was reminiscent of a young Waqar Younis as he took 4-148 in the first innings. Yet it was a mesmerising innings of 81 with the bat, featuring a joint-best nine sixes, which left an indelible impression.

Mohammad Ali - 5 - Hunted for wickets and beat the bat on a number of occasions but lacked the necessary consistency and control. Needs to iron out his no-ball issue which cost him Root's wicket in the second innings.

Muhammad Abbas - 7 - Pakistan's 'Mr Dependable' kept stoically plugging away as he shouldered much of the bowling burden for the tourists at the age of 36. Made useful lower-order runs to help force England to bat again, then got the ball talking on day four to give the hosts a fright.

title: England survive scare to sweep Pakistan series
description: England survive an almighty scare to eventually win the third Test against Pakistan by eight wickets and complete a 3-0 clean sweep.
fullText:
Third Rothesay Test, Edgbaston (day four of five)

Pakistan 133 (Tongue 4-42) & 449 (Masood 95, Razaullah 81, Babar 76, Awais 59)

England 453 (Brook 75, Smith 69, Lawrence 65, Gay 60, Robinson 50; Razaullah 4-148) & 130-2 (Root 62*, Cox 59*)

England won by eight wickets, won series 3-0

England survived an almighty scare to eventually win the third Test against Pakistan by eight wickets and complete a 3-0 clean sweep.

The home side were already facing an unexpected chase of 130 on the fourth day after being frazzled by the hitting of Pakistan debutant Razaullah on Friday evening.

And the prospect of one of Test cricket's greatest turnarounds was raised when England were reduced to 2-2 in the opening over. Ben Duckett edged Muhammad Abbas' first ball behind and Emilio Gay was palpably leg before.

England could have been 35-3 after Joe Root rashly dragged on to his own stumps off Mohammad Ali. Ali was found to have overstepped and Root was reprieved on 23.

While Root needed fortune, Jordan Cox once again impressed with a composed 59, a further claim for the Essex man to be in the XI for the first Test against South Africa in December.

Cox and Root shared an unbroken stand of 128, Root unbeaten on 62 when victory was sealed just before lunch.

For Root, this completes a successful return to the captaincy he resumed when Ben Stokes retired in June, while England end one of their most turbulent summers in history in a positive fashion.

They switch formats to begin a white-ball series against Sri Lanka in Southampton on Tuesday, with Brendon McCullum back in charge and Kevin Pietersen as part of the coaching staff.

Who has given selectors food for thought? England-Pakistan player ratings

Such was England's serene progress up to the third evening of the final Test of the series, it was easy to forget that they were without both a captain and a coach less than two months ago.

For all the good things they have done against Pakistan, there was the feeling their credentials had not been challenged by the dismal performances of the tourists.

When Pakistan were 0-2 in their second innings, England could have won in two days. From then on, the visitors finally found some fight and England were asked to respond. The way Root's side coped with the pressure was not entirely convincing.

Their tactics in the field collapsed in the face of Razaullah's assault on Friday, then their batting was wobbling on Saturday morning. An extra hundred runs on the target might have been difficult. How Pakistan will rue being dismissed for 133 on the first day.

It is to England's credit that they weathered the storm. Even if it took Pakistan two and a half matches to show up, England have still won three consecutive Tests after a previous run of two wins in 10.

Greater challenges await on the winter trips to South Africa, Bangladesh and Australia. New head coach Stephen Fleming arrives in the UK in the coming days with plenty in his in-tray.

One area of concern for Fleming will be England's openers, albeit if the modest returns of Duckett and Gay have come in a summer when ball has been on top of bat.

In a dramatic start to the day, Abbas' metronomic accuracy not only sent nerves through the England dressing room, but also further exposed a growing issue at the top of the order.

Duckett edged a beauty for a golden duck. Although he has registered England's only century of the summer, Duckett has not reached 20 in five innings against Pakistan and his average since the beginning of the Ashes is 23.

Gay has three half-centuries in his first summer as a Test cricketer, though being pinned on the shin by Abbas left his average below 25. Gay swished his bat in the direction of the stumps in frustration and wasted a review, his immediate future in the team vulnerable.

At 2-2, the pressure on England was as high as the tension among the modest Edgbaston crowd. That Cox was able to navigate the hosts to safety has massively boosted his chances of remaining when Jacob Bethell returns from injury, possibly at the expense of Gay.

Cox was more secure than his senior partner, Root. Not only did the captain survive the Ali no-ball, he also edged between the static slips off a furious Abbas when he had 34.

The miss sucked the hope from Pakistan and England were able to accelerate towards their target.

Bar the past 48 hours, this has been a shambolic series from Pakistan, who have been behind since Ollie Robinson trapped Azan Awais lbw from the first ball of the first Test at Headingley.

Pakistan threatened to abandon the second Test over an interview broadcast by Sky with the sons of Imran Khan. After the defeat at Lord's, they replaced head coach Sarfaraz Ahmed with Mike Hesson and dropped seven players from the squad - the ramifications of which look set to continue back at home.

There was a genuine chance of a two-day humiliation in Birmingham, so the Friday fightback was as welcome as it was unexpected. The top order finally found a way to cope with the England attack and Razaullah's pyrotechnics will live long in the memory.

Razaullah was one of the seven players called into the squad. He had already impressed with his pace bowling, dismissing Root in his first over in Test cricket, then the way he dismantled the England attack on Friday was thrilling and audacious.

Pakistan may have found a star in the making, a silver lining to a terrible tour.

title: Red Sea takeover demands ‘immediate response’: Retired Navy SEAL
description: Retired U.S. Navy SEAL Robert Harward lays out potential options now that Iranian-backed Houthis in Yemen have created a choke point in the Red Sea.
fullText:
(NewsNation) — Retired U.S. Navy SEAL Robert Harward, a former deputy commander of U.S. Central Command, laid out potential options now that Iranian-backed Houthis in Yemen have created a choke point in the Red Sea.

The capture of Perim Island located in the Bab el-Mandeb Strait (the Gate of Tears Strait) has made the war take on two fronts. The location of the island is crucial to controlling ship passage through the strait. The capture allows for the Houthis to be able to attack ships on both sides of the channels.

The island gives the Houthi's a line of sight on all targets, Harward said on "On Balance."

"All their weapons can range," he said. "Extra-small weapons can threaten those ships now, and it's very easy to put mines in from there. So, they can put a whole arsenal of weapons against every ship, and they can see them day and night. So, it's a big problem."

Harward believes that an immediate response is necessary and that it could potentially involve boots on the ground.

"They're not as well armed as the Iranians, so maybe this is an option," he said. "Not U.S., maybe Emirati, even Saudi. So, I believe in this case they need to bring the coalition together and act quickly to address this threat."

title: Safety checks on 20km of track to delay trains
description: Trains between Wickford and Southminster will be replaced by buses over the weekend.
fullText:
Rail passengers have been warned of delays in south Essex over the weekend because 20km (12.4 miles) of track is being assessed.

Network Rail said clay underneath the railway had "dried out and shrunk", causing issues with the track condition between Southminster and Wickford.

Buses will replace trains at all stations on the line on Saturday and Sunday, apart from at Battlesbridge where no rail replacement is being offered.

The area has been under intense scrutiny after a train carrying 62 passengers derailed near Wickford on 14 August.

Investigators believe the incident was caused by a "misalignment" or "kink" in the track and are due to release a full report at a later date.

Network Rail said despite recent rainfall, the ground would not immediately return to normal.

"In fact, as the clay reabsorbs water it can expand unevenly, causing further ground movement that can affect the track," a spokesman said.

Trains have been running at slower speeds along the Southminster branch and with an amended timetable since the derailment.

Engineers plan to use stone ballast to create a solid foundation underneath the track.

Martin Beable, Great British Railways Anglia's chief operating officer, apologised for the disruption.

"These are essential works that we must get done to keep running a safe railway that passengers can depend on," he said.

title: Opinion - For many Democrats this cycle, the tipping point between victory and defeat is Israel
description: Beneath their putative “big tent,” the national Democratic Party is embroiled in an ideological civil war — one that is likely to intensify through 2028's presidential campaign.
fullText:
Beneath their putative big tent, the national Democratic Party is embroiled in an ideological civil war that is likely to intensify through the 2028 presidential campaign.

While there are many topic Democrats disagree on — socialism, transgender issues, open borders and appeals to the white working class — the one that underlies this battle for the party's soul is U.S. support for Israel.

"The genocide in Gaza has had an overwhelming effect on large, significant segments of the American public," said Ian Lustick, co-author of the new book, "Israel's Lobby: America in the Grip of a Foreign Power." "Israel's policies in the past 20 years have become essentially indefensible."

For Jews critical of the Netanyahu regime, the horrific Oct. 7 Hamas attack (1,200 Israelis killed; hundreds taken hostage) did not justify killing thousands of Gaza civilians or targeting journalists and emergency medical personal with supposedly precision air strikes.

For single-issue, pro-Likud Jews, having a Democratic Party united against further U.S. aid to Israel means they would rather have a JD Vance or Marco Rubio in the White House, and a Republican-controlled Congress.

In U.S. Senate races in Michigan and Georgia, pro-Likud activists are supporting Republican campaigns.

Shocked by Abdul El-Sayed's Democratic primary victory, prominent Detroit businessman Eric Bronstein — a Democrat — wrote an open letter to Jewish Democrats and independents in support of Republican Senate candidate and former Rep. Mike Rogers (R-Mich.). Several Jewish Democratic bundlers later met for a Rogers fundraiser.

Other Michigan Jewish Democrats, like Attorney General Dana Nessel, disagree, declining to endorse Rogers. "We have a moral imperative to place the needs of the world above even our own self-interest and, yes, even our own survival," she told a gathering of Jewish Democrats, provoking Likud supporters' outrage.

In Georgia, in an open letter to Sen. Jon Ossoff (D) — Jewish, up for reelection and a possible 2028 presidential aspirant — Atlanta Jewish Times publisher Michael Morris called on Ossoff to "stop lying to me and your constituents" about his "ironclad support for Israel. ... Your antagonism toward Israel has remained steadfast."

El-Sayed and Ossoff recently rejected controversial Twitch streamer Hasan Piker's alleged antisemitic postings. That was insufficient and too late, legacy Jewish organizations said.

In Florida's U.S. Senate primary, state Rep. Angie Nixon (D), a democratic socialist, has repeatedly accused Israel of committing genocide. She criticized the favorite for the nomination, Alex Vindman, for silence on Israel. She introduced a bill in the Florida legislature calling for a "de-escalation and ceasefire in the state of Israel and occupied Palestine," supports cutting U.S. aid for the Jewish state and refuses AIPAC money. Nixon's position on military aid to Israel helped her upset win.

Across the country, accepting AIPAC money has proved toxic for many congressional candidates. For decades, AIPAC threw its weight (and money) around with supplicants. But in insurgent primary campaigns this year, accepting AIPAC-sourced campaign money has become a liability.

Rogers's campaign in Michigan is nervous, asking AIPAC to lie low and routing the cash from its superPAC, United Democracy Project, to a separate non-campaign group. Notwithstanding, Jewish Insider reports that Rogers attended four AIPAC fundraisers in Los Angeles over a long weekend in late August.

Even in deep-red Oklahoma, one candidate in the Senate Democratic primary ran a social media spot featuring a giant red bin labeled "AIPAC Funds," with a caption reading, "Just taking out the trash." The candidate, N'kiyla Jasmine Thomas, trounced her pro-Israel opponent, centrist Jim Priest.

Of course, there are still some imponderable "ifs" ahead. If, for example, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is turned out of office in October, that may affect U.S. Israel supporters' internal debates.

Ironically, approaching the fall midterms, Democrats are much less divided than current struggles over Israel would suggest. From the center-left Democratic governors of swing states who support Israel, like Pennsylvania's Josh Shapiro, to progressives like Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez of New York City, consensus exists on November's campaign agenda: economics, affordability, Medicare for All, higher federal minimum wage, free preschool and no AI data centers.

I have a modest proposal for Democrats: Put off this searing fratricidal controversy over Israel until after the midterms. Don't fight over the spoils of victory until there is a victory to fight over.

Mark I. Pinsky is a journalist and author based in Durham, N.C. He was a civilian volunteer attached to the IDF in El Arish, Sinai, in the summer of 1967.

title: Major companies to cut back on 2027 health benefits in blow to workers
description: Disney and Starbucks are among firms cutting health benefits for 2027 as medical costs continue to soar. This trend may mean you'll pay more.
fullText:
Health benefits are a top factor in whether Americans take or stay in a job, yet in a span of a few weeks, a handful of large employers reportedly are planning cutbacks or changes that can make that choice even tougher in 2027.

Walt Disney, Bloomberg, Starbucks, Deloitte, and the City of Dallas are among those taking actions next year to rein in health care spending, from restricting spousal coverage to eliminating plan options or cutting drug benefits to deal with soaring costs. Health plans are projecting the highest medical cost trend in nearly two decades, with commercial health care costs expected to rise 9% in 2027, according to consulting firm PwC. Insurer Aon predicted even higher costs, with U.S. employer health care costs increasing 9.5% next year, pushing average costs above $19,000 per employee.

These benefit cuts could be devastating for workers if they have to shoulder more of their own health costs, analysts said. Americans already say they have limited budgets for health insurance outside an employer-sponsored plan, according to finance researcher ValuePenguin. Overall, 42% of the 2,001 adults surveyed in July said they could comfortably afford less than $100 a month, while 23% said they could afford between $100 and $249.

"Health insurance is much more than a minor perk for most working Americans," said Maggie Gunara, senior staff writer at ValuePenguin, in a report. "Among those who are employed or job hunting, 87% say the health plan attached to a job matters at least somewhat when they're deciding whether to take a job or stick around."

Some of the companies making cuts include:

Walt Disney Co. will stop covering working spouses under its health care plan in 2027 if those spouses have access to coverage through their own employers. The change applies to the company's more than 200,000 U.S. employees.

Starbucks surprised workers when open enrollment began by nearly doubling the price tag for health insurance for some workers and lowering the share of employer contribution to the cost. It's also ending coverage for GLP-1 weight loss drugs, beginning in October.

Bloomberg LP plans to make its employees start paying monthly premium contributions for the first time in the company's history.

Deloitte will halve paid parental leave to eight weeks for workers in its "Center" talent segment, which covers internal IT, finance, and administrative functions, effective Jan. 1. It's also ending for those workers its $50,000 adoption and surrogacy reimbursement program, which also covered IVF-related costs, as well as pension accruals after Dec. 31.

The Dallas City Council will vote on Sept. 16 on a proposal to eliminate its copay insurance plan and end GLP-1 coverage for employees using the medication for weight loss.
